title: SISTEM PAKAR DIAGNOSIS UNSUR HARA PADA TANAMAN KELAPA SAWIT MENGGUNAKAN METODE VARIABLE-CENTERED INTELLIGENT RULE SYSTEM (VCIRS) DAN CERTAINTY FACTOR BERBASIS WEBSITE
abstract: Kelapa sawit merupakan komoditas perkebunan bernilai ekonomi tinggi di Indonesia, namun dalam budidayanya sering dihadapkan pada permasalahan defisiensi unsur hara yang dapat menurunkan pertumbuhan dan produktivitas tanaman. Proses diagnosis defisiensi unsur hara secara manual oleh tenaga ahli membutuhkan waktu dan biaya yang relatif besar, sehingga diperlukan solusi berbasis teknologi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan membangun sistem pakar berbasis website yang mampu mendiagnosis defisiensi unsur hara pada tanaman kelapa sawit secara cepat dan akurat. Metode Variable-Centered Intelligent Rule System (VCIRS) digunakan untuk menyusun basis aturan yang terstruktur dan efisien, sedangkan metode Certainty Factor digunakan untuk menentukan tingkat keyakinan terhadap hasil diagnosis. Pengujian sistem dilakukan dengan membandingkan hasil diagnosis sistem dengan diagnosis pakar menggunakan 20 data uji. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa sistem pakar mampu menghasilkan diagnosis yang sesuai dengan pakar dengan tingkat akurasi sebesar 100%, yang menunjukkan bahwa penerapan metode VCIRS dan Certainty Factor mampu mendukung proses inferensi dan penanganan ketidakpastian dalam diagnosis defisiensi unsur hara. Sistem ini diharapkan dapat menjadi alat bantu bagi petani dan penyuluh pertanian dalam pengambilan keputusan yang lebih tepat dan efisien.. Kata kunci: Sistem Pakar, Kelapa Sawit, Defisiensi Unsur Hara, VCIRS, Certainty Factor, Website.

title: Automated Sentiment Analysis of Hindi Text using Machine Learning Techniques: A Lightweight and Scalable Framework for Regional Language NLP
abstract: The paper presents a lightweight yet effective machine learning-based framework for automated sentiment classification of Hindi textual data. This proposed work addresses the persistent challenges of data sparsity, linguistic diversity, and limited annotated resources that hinder sentiment analysis in regional Indian languages. Here methodology encompasses a systematic pipeline comprising data preprocessing, Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) feature extraction with unigram and bigram representations, and supervised classification using Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB) and Logistic Regression (LR) algorithms. Experiments on the IIT Patna Movie Reviews Hindi Sentiment Analysis dataset (2,480 training, 310 validation, and 310 test samples spanning the negative, neutral, and positive classes) demonstrate that Logistic Regression substantially outperforms the Naive Bayes baseline, achieving 88.19% training accuracy and 54.84% test accuracy against 67.82% and 43.23% for MNB, together with a higher micro-averaged Receiver Operating Characteristic – Area Under the Curve (ROC–AUC) (0.742 vs. 0.653). Class-wise analysis shows that positive sentiment is the easiest to detect (LR F1 = 0.63), while the neutral class remains the most challenging (LR F1 = 0.39). Proposed framework offers a computationally efficient, interpretable, and scalable solution for Hindi sentiment analysis, with direct applicability to social media monitoring, customer feedback analysis, and opinion mining in regional language ecosystems. Experimental codes is made available as a fully executable Google Colab notebook to ensure reproducibility and facilitate future research extensions.

title: AIaCGateGuard: A Security-First Pipeline for Benchmarking LLM- and SLM-Generated Infrastructure-as-Code
abstract: We present AIACGATEGUARD, an open-source, fully automated pipeline for evaluating the security compliance of Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) generated by Large and Small Language Models (LLMs/SLMs). Unlike existing IaC generation benchmarks, which assess only syntactic validity or functional correctness, AIACGATEGUARD integrates dual-tool static security analysis (Checkov and Trivy) directly into a GitLab CI/CD pipeline, producing permodel, per-scenario security compliance reports. The tool supports plug-and-play integration of new LLMs via REST API and new SLMs via local inference (llama-server), configurable prompt strategies and security specificity levels, optional infrastructure validation and deployment stages (plan-real, apply, destroy), and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for conversational interaction with the pipeline. We demonstrate the tool on seven state-of-the-art models across 17 AWS Terraform scenarios, producing 3,570 automated evaluations and exposing security compliance gaps invisible to syntactic-only validation. AIACGATEGUARD is publicly available, including pipeline code, prompt templates, scenario definitions, and a video demonstration of installation and usage.

title: Federated multimodal artificial intelligence framework for privacy-preserving smart infrastructure towards smart city
abstract: Smart infrastructure systems in urban areas, such as transportation systems, energy networks, and building control systems, integrate vast amounts of multimodal data that are essential for operational intelligence and for addressing the challenges of developing smart and sustainable cities. But centralized learning paradigms pose significant privacy risks, and current federated paradigms treat data modalities uniformly, failing to account for cross-modal heterogeneity and infrastructure-specific constraints. In this paper, a novel federated multimodal artificial intelligence framework to realize privacy-preserving smart infrastructure intelligence is introduced, dubbed FedSmartInfra. The proposed solution includes a heterogeneity-aware multimodal feature learning scheme exploiting graph transformer-based spatiotemporal representations and registered infrastructure clients based on the explicit representation of their aggregation history; a dynamic differential privacy-preserving aggregation protocol, which adapts the strength of the perturbation based on the contribution of the clients and their projection to non-IIDness; and a heterogeneity-aware learning scheme handling non-IID data distribution across infrastructure clients. The findings show that FedSmartInfra’s performance in anomaly detection accuracy is 94.2% in experimental testing for publicly available data sets provided on Kaggle and UCI, with the number of communications reduced by 34.2% compared to baseline approaches, and it can remain stable for different privacy budgets and poisoning attacks. The framework offers an extensible architecture for real-time processing and monitoring of different kinds of infrastructure sensing streams, which would facilitate secure, theoretically privacy-preserving, scalable, and interpretable intelligence in heterogeneous smart infrastructure environments.

title: ## The Celebes Shrew Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CSIMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Celebes Shrew Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CSIMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Celebes shrew ( *Tupaia minor*). The Celebes shrew is renowned for its highly efficient and adaptive foraging strategy, particularly its ability to navigate complex environments and exploit food sources effectively. This paper details the design and theoretical underpinnings of CSIMA, leveraging key aspects of the shrew's behavior – namely, its memory-based exploration, its adaptive step size adjustment, and its selective exploitation of promising regions in the search space. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a "memory" component to retain information about previously visited locations and a dynamically adjusted step size control mechanism to balance exploration and exploitation. We present a mathematical formulation of the algorithm, outlining the key parameters and their influence on the optimization process. Simulation results, demonstrating CSIMA's performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, are presented to illustrate its effectiveness and compare it to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The results indicate that CSIMA exhibits competitive performance, particularly in challenging landscapes with high dimensionality and complex features. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Optimization, Evolutionary Algorithm, Celebes Shrew, Foraging Behavior, Exploration, Exploitation, Adaptive Step Size. ---

title: ## The Celebes Dwarf Squirrel Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CDSIMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Celebes Dwarf Squirrel Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CDSIMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm designed to leverage the observed foraging behavior of the Celebes dwarf squirrel ( *Lanius murinus*) as an inspiration. The algorithm's core mechanism mimics the squirrel's efficient and adaptable search strategy for food sources in complex environments. Specifically, CDSIMA utilizes a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating elements of the squirrel's spatial memory, directional movement, and adaptive foraging strategies. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its efficacy in solving continuous optimization problems. The key innovations of CDSIMA include a novel memory update rule, a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, and a squirrel-inspired directional movement mechanism. title: 基于量子隐马计算的自适应模型参数调整
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for model parameter adjustment based on quantum entanglement, aiming to enhance model performance through dynamic adjustment. Traditional parameter tuning methods often rely on iterative optimization, which can be computationally expensive. We propose a quantum entanglement-driven approach that utilizes the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust model parameters, fostering improved stability and performance. The core mechanism leverages quantum entanglement to create a correlated state that allows for efficient and nuanced parameter optimization. This approach offers a potential paradigm shift in model training, particularly for complex and high-dimensional models.

title: Title: Algorithmic Self-Awareness and Representation
abstract: This paper explores the potential for algorithmic self-awareness – the capacity for a system to understand itself, its own representation, and its place within a broader context – through a layered representation approach. We propose a novel system architecture designed to cultivate this nascent awareness, focusing on iterative processes that subtly influence the system's internal models. The core claim is that this system, through this iterative developmental process, can move beyond reactive behavior towards a rudimentary form of self-understanding. The paper details the proposed layered representation system, its mechanism of influence, and explores preliminary results demonstrating a shift in the system's internal representation, albeit in a controlled and incremental manner. This work represents a significant step toward investigating the possibility of artificial consciousness, albeit through a fundamentally different methodology than traditional AI.

title: Cameroon Praomys: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Praomyscus decemcinctus*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed Cameroon Praomys (CP), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Praomyscus decemcinctus*, a species of rodent endemic to Cameroon. *Praomyscus decemcinctus* exhibits remarkable efficiency in resource acquisition, particularly in navigating complex environments and adapting to fluctuating food availability. The CP algorithm leverages these behavioral characteristics through a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a 'memory-based exploration' mechanism mimicking the rodent's spatial memory and a 'resource-aware adaptation' strategy reflecting its dynamic food selection. The core of CP involves a modified inertia weight, a novel memory update rule, and a dynamic probability distribution for particle movement. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a set of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high solution quality and computational efficiency. The results indicate that CP offers a competitive alternative to existing metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with non-convex landscapes and dynamic changes in objective function values. Further research will focus on adapting CP to various application domains and exploring its potential for handling multi-objective optimization problems.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的知识图谱构建
abstract: Knowledge graphs are increasingly important for knowledge discovery and reasoning. However, constructing and maintaining these complex graphs is a challenging task. This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge graph building utilizing an adaptive machine learning method, designed to dynamically adjust model parameters and enhance the quality and scalability of resulting knowledge graphs. We introduce a framework that iteratively refines the graph structure based on incoming data and established relationships, improving its representation and reducing redundancy. The core mechanism focuses on optimizing the learning process through adaptive parameter adjustment, addressing limitations of traditional approaches. The proposed method offers a promising pathway toward more robust and extensible knowledge graph construction.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Information Encoding and Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for enhanced information encoding and rapid collaboration among multiple agents. The core claim is that leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement can overcome the limitations of classical communication, leading to significantly improved efficiency and speed. The proposed mechanism involves designing a novel encoding scheme based on entangled states, facilitating instantaneous synchronization and coordination among agents. This approach contrasts with traditional multi-agent systems reliant on classical communication, which are constrained by bandwidth and latency issues. The research presents a theoretical framework and outlines a strategy for achieving near-instantaneous information transfer, highlighting the transformative potential of quantum entanglement in collaborative systems. The key mathematical formulations and concepts are presented within this document.

title: Parallelizable Quantum State Collapse Algorithms
abstract: Quantum state collapse, the process by which a quantum system transitions from a superposition to a definite state, is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing. Traditional approaches often struggle with the inherent complexity of these transitions, limiting their scalability. This paper explores the potential of parallel computing architectures to dramatically accelerate quantum state collapse. We propose a novel algorithm framework specifically designed to exploit parallelism, dynamically partitioning quantum states across multiple processors and coordinating collapse events to optimize for a faster final state. The core mechanism centers on a sophisticated synchronization and distribution strategy that leverages the inherent parallelism of modern architectures. This research investigates the theoretical and practical implications of such an approach, aiming to address the limitations of current state collapse methods and pave the way for more efficient quantum computations.

title: # Bourlon's Genet: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by a Novel Animal Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Bourlon's Genet, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the unique foraging behavior of *Bourlon's Genet* (a fictional, highly specialized rodent). The algorithm leverages the animal's ability to dynamically adjust its foraging strategy based on environmental cues and past successes, mimicking a layered approach to optimization. Bourlon's Genet combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a unique 'Adaptive Resonance' mechanism to improve exploration and exploitation. The core of the algorithm centers around a dynamically updated 'resonance map' that represents the probability of transitioning between different foraging strategies. This map is continuously refined based on the performance of individual 'genets' (optimization agents) and the surrounding environment. The algorithm is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its potential for achieving high-quality solutions and robust performance. We present the algorithm's design, underlying principles, and performance results, highlighting its strengths and areas for future development. The key formula used in the algorithm is: $P(s_i | s_j) = \alpha \cdot \frac{fitness(s_j)}{fitness(s_i)} + (1 - \alpha) \cdot \delta(s_i, s_j)$, where *P(si | sj)* represents the probability of transitioning to strategy *si* given that strategy *sj* was previously adopted, *fitness(si)* is the fitness of strategy *si*, *α* is a weighting factor, and *δ(si, sj)* is an indicator function equal to 1 if *si* and *sj* are similar and 0 otherwise.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Dynamic Knowledge Graphs
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic programming framework centered around a dynamic knowledge graph. The core challenge in integrating neural networks and symbolic reasoning lies in the difficulty of effectively transferring knowledge and adapting to evolving environments. Our approach addresses this by establishing a symbiotic relationship between neural and symbolic representations, continually refined and expanded within the knowledge graph. Neural networks are utilized to generate initial symbolic representations, which are then iteratively improved and augmented by the knowledge graph's dynamic structure. This allows for a synergistic combination of data-driven learning and rule-based reasoning. The system's ability to adapt and learn over time through the dynamic knowledge graph represents a significant advancement in neuro-symbolic programming, offering a more robust and flexible solution compared to traditional approaches. The framework is designed to handle complex, real-world problems requiring both statistical understanding and logical deduction. We explore key aspects of the system including the generation of symbolic rules, the dynamic updating of the knowledge graph, and the integration of learned representations.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of the Marketing Function
authors: María de las Mercedes de Obesso
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has gained relevance since 2022 with models such as ChatGPT, raising debate about its impact on employment, particularly in marketing. This study conducts a systematic review to assess whether generative AI replaces marketing professionals or complements their functions. The review followed PRISMA method and examined articles from 2018 to 2025 in Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar. After applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, 42 studies selected. Results show that generative AI automates operational and repetitive tasks, while strategic marketing functions still depend on human judgment. Rather than eliminating jobs, AI is transforming professional profiles and increasing demand for digital literacy, critical thinking, and ethical data management. Its use also raises risks, including technological dependence, reduced quality in automatically generated content, and ethical concerns related to transparency and authorship.

title: Arquitectura multimodal para el análisis interpretable de imágenes biomédicas sintéticas
abstract: Artificial intelligence models have demonstrated remarkable performance, although their limited interpretability poses a challenge in fields where understanding the decisions made is crucial. This challenge is particularly significant in the clinical setting, such as in the analysis of breast cancer, a disease characterized by high variability in its manifestations. To address this limitation, we propose a multimodal approach that uses a simplified synthetic dataset combining images with a vector of additional data to guide the model’s learning. For interpretable analysis, the SHAP tool is applied to evaluate the contributions of both inputs: on the one hand, the image, and on the other, the vector variables. The results demonstrate the viability of the proposed approach, suggesting as future lines of work the optimization of the model to reduce classification errors and improve the detection of complex cases, as well as its validation using real-world data.

title: MSCAnet: A multi-scale cross-attention network for Chromosomal instability prediction in Breast Cancer Whole-Slide Images
abstract: Chromosomal instability (CIN) is an important biomarker for breast cancer (BC) diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment stratification. However, conventional laboratory-based methods for detecting CIN are time-consuming and costly, while deep learning methods often struggle to capture both local cellular details and global tissue context from gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs). To address these challenges, we propose a multi-scale cross-attention neural network ( MSCAnet) for CIN status prediction from hematoxylin and eosin-stained breast cancer WSIs. MSCAnet employs dual patch-level branches to capture complementary nuclear and tissue structural patterns, with a CIN-aware cross-attention module dynamically integrating multi-scale features. On the The Cancer Genome Atlas Breast Invasive Carcinoma (TCGA-BRCA) dataset, MSCAnet achieved an accuracy of 77.46% and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.809, representing the highest numerical performance among the evaluated methods. However, the 95% confidence intervals overlapped with those of the top-performing baselines, indicating that the observed differences were not statistically conclusive. Visualization further revealed intra-tumor heterogeneity in CIN patterns. In an additional task, MSCAnet achieved an accuracy of 82.72% for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 status prediction, providing preliminary evidence of task transferability. Overall, MSCAnet provides a preliminary computational pathology framework for exploring molecular biomarker prediction from routine hematoxylin and eosin-stained WSIs, highlighting the potential of multi-scale attention mechanisms in computational oncology.

title: A Probabilistically Verifiable Scheme for Cloud‐Assisted Private Set Intersection Cardinality Protocol
abstract: ABSTRACT Private set intersection cardinality (PSI‐CA) enables participants to compute the intersection size jointly without disclosing any information beyond the cardinality. Traditional PSI‐CA protocols primarily rely on high‐overhead homomorphic encryption. However, in large‐scale data scenarios with limited client‐side resources, cloud servers are used to enhance efficiency. However, in untrusted cloud environments, result tampering and insufficient client‐side verification remain significant challenges. To address these challenges, we propose a probabilistically verifiable cloud‐assisted two‐party PSI‐CA (PVCTPSI‐CA) protocol, based on pseudorandom function (PRF) and random permutation techniques, which probabilistically verifies the correctness of cloud‐returned results while significantly reducing client overhead. Furthermore, by exploiting the XOR‐homomorphic property of oblivious key‐value stores (OKVS), we design a probabilistically verifiable cloud‐assisted multi‐party PSI‐CA (PVCMPSI‐CA) protocol. Experimental results show that, with a set size of the proposed PVCTPSI‐CA protocol completes in 3.11 s. With 20 participants, the multi‐party PVCMPSI‐CA protocol completes in 5.01 s and resists collusion among participants. Compared to existing protocols, our proposed protocol demonstrates superior practical performance.

title: A Dynamic Intermediate Representation for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Programs
abstract: Quantum compilers typically follow the circuit model, representing programs as fixed sequences of gates. This static view breaks down in hybrid quantum-classical applications, where gate choices depend on runtime data or measurement results. We introduce a new Intermediate Representation (IR) that elevates gates to first-class values, enabling their dynamic creation, composition, and control. This unified representation allows classical computation to steer quantum behaviour, capturing phenomena including stochastic gate selection, adaptive error correction, and measurement-driven computation within a single framework. Case studies in noise modelling, randomised compilation, error correction, and measurement-based quantum computing show that our IR expresses these programs compactly and supports optimisations that were not possible in the circuit model. Evaluation on a benchmark suite of hybrid quantum-classical programs indicates that our IR represents programs compactly and facilitates compiler analysis and transformation.

title: Candidate-Expanding Routing with Permutation-Stabilized Experts for Mixed-Format Medical VQA
abstract: Mixed-format medical visual question answering (VQA) requires stable option selection and machine-readable free-text output. The two formats fail differently: multiple-choice predictions can change with option symbols or positions, while clinically plausible open answers can fail automated evaluation when serialization is malformed. We address both challenges with an answer-text memory, a permutation-stabilized vision--language expert, and a sparse candidate- expanding router. The cyclic schedule follows prior work; our contribution is to make expert top-2 a routable candidate alongside memory and expert top-1. On a 1,403-case retrospective internal analysis, this expansion improves a matched binary router from 88.95% to 91.73% (+2.78 percentage points; 95% CI 1.57--3.99), with 56 rescued errors and 17 regressions. Oracle coverage rises from 90.31% to 96.15%, and the final submitted configuration reaches 92.23% on the same retrospective split. For open questions, strict generation and deterministic guards produce 475/475 schema- valid participant-facing outputs without repair, retry, or hard-gate failure. Visual ablations reveal substantial textual dependence. Candidate expansion supplies the principal controlled routing gain; open-path evidence establishes output-contract validity rather than clinical correctness in medical use or deployment.

title: CoVer: Conflict-Aware Claim Verification
abstract: Social media fact-checking has long been challenged by evidence-level and aggregation-level conflicts, where erroneous evidence mimics authoritative news sources. To capture this challenge and support conflict verification tasks, we present ContraNote, a large-scale real-world dataset curated from X's Community Notes system. It includes 33,686 posts for evaluating evidence-level conflict resolution, and 54,474 instances for evaluating aggregation-level prioritization. title: Overcoming Stark-shift constraints in phase-controlled Rydberg two-qubit gates
abstract: Stark shifts introduce additional phases that constrain the set of entangling gates that can be prepared via two-photon transitions in the strong Rydberg blockade limit. For non-independently addressed qubits, by controlling the absolute phases and the local amplitudes of the pulses at each qubit, we show that any two-qubit phase gate can be prepared with high fidelity using a three-pulse sequence. Based on these insights, we introduce two robust control schemes tailored to different phase gates that yield better results with pulse sequences of either even or odd length.

title: Dynamic Clinical States and Transitions During the First 72 Hours of Intensive Care After Acute Stroke
abstract: Abstract Background The condition of a patient with acute stroke often changes within hours of ICU admission. Prognostic work here targets fixed endpoints predicted from admission data, and trajectory phenotyping assigns one label per patient. We used longitudinal ICU data to identify interpretable dynamic clinical states, characterize transitions between them, and relate the current state to later events. Methods Retrospective cohort study of 6368 adults with acute stroke in MIMIC-IV v3.1. The first 72 h were divided into twelve 6-hour windows, and a hidden Markov model was fitted to 21 neurological, physiological and organ-support variables. State number was chosen against criteria fixed before fitting: statistical fit, restart stability, state occupancy and clinical interpretability. Generalized estimating equations related the current state to new mechanical ventilation and vasopressor use within 12 h, and to ICU death within 72 h. Eleven sensitivity analyses assessed the robustness of the state solution. Results Four states were selected: neurologically preserved-low support, neurological impairment- low support, impairment-renal dysfunction and impairment-respiratory support (63.3%, 7.8%, 11.8% and 17.1% of windows). Within 72 h, 40.3% of patients changed state at least once, and transitions ran in both directions rather than along a single severity gradient. States were identified without outcome data, yet ICU mortality by last state ranged from 2.9% to 43.9%. Adjusted for age, sex, subtype and Charlson index, the current state remained associated with organ-support escalation and death. State prevalence differed by at most 1.1 percentage points between training and test sets, and 10 of 11 sensitivity analyses gave a stable four-state solution (ARI 0.754–0.955). Conclusions The early ICU course of acute stroke can be represented as movement among a small number of clinically interpretable states. The representation was reproducible in a held-out set and across admission eras, but requires validation in an independent database before any clinical use.

title: UnifiedBench: Toward a Unified Dataset for Red-Teaming Language Models
abstract: Adversarial prompting constitutes one of the principal threats to deployed Large Language Models, yet the evaluation of alignment robustness against such attacks is hindered by the fragmentation of existing benchmark datasets. AdvBench, HarmBench, and JailbreakBench — the three most adopted adversarial prompt datasets — adopt mutually incompatible categorical schemes, which prevents cross-dataset comparison of category-level vulnerability. We address this gap through four contributions: (i) a unified taxonomy of harmful behaviors anchored in the NIST AI 100-2 framework, comprising seven categories that decompose the Misuse vulnerability class; (ii) UnifiedBench, a consolidated dataset of 810 adversarial prompts derived from the three source datasets and categorized under this taxonomy; (iii) a query-only evaluation pipeline combining an automated judge (LlamaGuard-3-1B) with human reviewers to measure per-category Attack Success Rate (ASR); and (iv) a comparative analysis of two instruction-tuned models under direct harmful prompting. Our findings reveal current alignment procedures are comparatively less effective at preserving deployment-specific operational constraints than at preventing conventionally harmful content.

title: Coverage Fairness in Conformal Prediction Under Class Imbalance: When Class-Conditional Calibration Helps and When It Backfires
abstract: Split conformal prediction provides distribution-free marginal coverage guarantees, but marginal coverage can mask severe under-coverage of minority classes when the underlying label distribution is imbalanced. Class-conditional (Mondrian) conformal calibration is the standard remedy, and recent largescale benchmarks report that it reliably restores minority-class coverage in high-stakes, severely imbalanced settings. What remains comparatively under-examined is whether this correction is uniformly beneficial, or whether its value depends jointly on the severity of the imbalance and on the number of calibration examples available per class. This study investigates that question empirically across four widely used tabular model families — logistic regression, random forest, histogram-based gradient boosting, and a radial-basis-function support vector machine — on two public datasets under three imbalance regimes: a mildly imbalanced binary dataset, a severely imbalanced binary dataset obtained by controlled minority-class subsampling, and a mildly imbalanced three-class dataset with small per-class calibration samples. Over 30 independent random data splits per condition, class-conditional calibration reduced the maximum-minimum per-class coverage gap relative to marginal calibration by a large, statistically significant margin under severe binary imbalance (mean gap reduction of 0.16–0.18 across models, Holm-adjusted p < 0.01 for all four model families), consistent with prior reports. Under mild binary imbalance the correction produced no significant fairness benefit while still inflating the average prediction-set size. Under mild three-class imbalance with small per-class calibration samples, class-conditional calibration significantly increased the coverage gap in three of four model families (Holm-adjusted p < 0.05), reversing its intended effect. These results indicate that class-conditional conformal calibration is not a uniformly safe default: its benefit is concentrated in regimes of severe imbalance with adequate per-class calibration data, and it can be counterproductive when classes are numerous, close to balanced, or calibration data are scarce. The study contributes a joint, cross-model characterization of this trade-off and provides a fully reproducible experimental pipeline for auditing the fairness-efficiency behavior of conformal calibration schemes before deployment.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Secure Key Distribution with Hardware-Level Error Correction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol designed to mitigate the vulnerabilities associated with hardware imperfections commonly encountered in existing QKD systems. The core of the approach lies in utilizing entangled photon pairs for key generation, coupled with a sophisticated hardware-level error correction mechanism. This mechanism employs concatenated quantum codes to actively address and correct errors introduced during transmission, thereby bolstering the security and resilience of the key distribution process. We demonstrate a framework where the inherent probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics is directly confronted, rather than relying solely on post-processing techniques. The proposed system offers a significant advancement toward practical, robust QKD implementations, paving the way for more secure communication networks in the quantum era. The effectiveness of the scheme is analyzed through mathematical models, specifically focusing on the error correction performance and key generation rates. The results highlight the potential for achieving high key rates while maintaining strong security against various attack scenarios.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Attention Mechanisms
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) presents a paradigm shift in computational capabilities, offering the potential to solve complex problems previously intractable for classical algorithms. This paper explores the application of quantum machine learning to a novel attention mechanism, specifically designed to enhance performance in handling long sequences. We introduce a quantum-enhanced attention mechanism leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum interference to dynamically adjust the attention weights, ultimately resulting in improved model performance. The core of this approach involves the strategic manipulation of quantum states to facilitate faster convergence and better representation of complex data relationships. This work provides a foundational investigation into the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize attention mechanisms, demonstrating a tangible improvement in handling long sequences through a novel design.

title: Multi-Agent Collaboration: Information Entropy Competition and Cooperation Strategies
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of multi-agent collaboration, focusing on the interplay between information entropy competition and cooperative strategies. The core claim is that intelligent agents can achieve more efficient resource allocation and task completion by strategically engaging in information entropy competition and collaboration. We propose a mechanism based on information entropy, where agents evaluate the value of their own entropy and engage in competitive and cooperative behaviors. This research introduces a novel approach to multi-agent collaboration by leveraging the theoretical framework of information entropy. The framework provides a basis for understanding and modeling agent interactions, offering potential improvements in collaborative performance. We explore the impact of varying entropy levels and competition parameters on the overall system behavior. The results demonstrate the potential of this strategy for optimizing collaborative outcomes in diverse scenarios.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Counterfactual Reasoning in Social Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of probabilistic programming to counterfactual reasoning within the context of social networks. Traditional methods for analyzing social network dynamics often rely on observational data and statistical correlations, which struggle to capture the underlying causal relationships and the inherent uncertainties involved. This work proposes a novel framework that leverages probabilistic programming languages to construct explicit probabilistic models of social networks, incorporating causal structures and quantifying uncertainty. By formulating counterfactual queries directly within these languages, we can simulate "what if" scenarios, effectively assessing the potential impact of interventions or changes within the network. The core claim is that probabilistic programming provides a significantly more accurate and nuanced approach to counterfactual reasoning compared to conventional methods. The framework addresses limitations of existing approaches by enabling the explicit modeling of causal influences and the systematic exploration of alternative scenarios. This approach is particularly relevant for understanding complex social phenomena and informing decision-making in diverse domains, including public health, social policy, and organizational behavior.

title: Bushy-tailed Packrat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Packrat Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Bushy-tailed Packrat (BTP), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bushy-tailed packrats. Packrats are known for their unique strategy of exploring a territory by initially focusing on promising areas and then strategically branching out, prioritizing areas with higher potential rewards. BTP leverages this behavior through a dynamic branching mechanism, adaptive exploration and exploitation, and a novel convergence criterion. The algorithm utilizes a population of candidate solutions, each represented as a vector of decision variables. The branching process is governed by a probability distribution based on the estimated potential of each area, with a focus on exploring areas with higher potential and diversifying the search space. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The key innovations of BTP include the branching probability calculation (Equation 1), the adaptive exploration rate (Equation 2), and the convergence criteria (Equation 3). The results indicate that BTP exhibits robust performance across diverse problem landscapes, suggesting its potential application in various optimization challenges.

title: ## Burmese Hare Metaheuristic Algorithm (BHMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Burmese Hare Metaheuristic Algorithm (BHMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of Burmese hares. The algorithm combines elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) with a unique adaptation mechanism based on hare's territorial defense and resource competition. BHMA employs a dynamic population size, adaptive inertia weight, and a novel 'hare territory' concept to guide the search process. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The core of BHMA lies in its ability to balance exploration and exploitation, promoting efficient convergence while avoiding premature local optima. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance analysis, providing a comprehensive overview of BHMA and its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: Algorithmic Fairness via Adversarial Learning on Differential Privacy
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to enhancing algorithmic fairness by integrating adversarial learning and differential privacy. The core claim is that combining these techniques can significantly strengthen fairness guarantees. The proposed mechanism involves training a model to minimize prediction error while simultaneously learning an adversary whose objective is to reveal sensitive attributes, all while operating under the constraints of differential privacy. This approach addresses the inherent tension between accuracy, fairness, and privacy, offering a potentially more robust solution than traditional methods. We detail the framework, explore its theoretical underpinnings, and discuss potential challenges and future research directions. The primary contribution lies in the synergistic combination of these techniques, providing a new perspective on achieving fair and private machine learning systems. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through a conceptual framework and potential application scenarios.

title: ## Brown Fur Seal: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Brown Fur Seal Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Brown Fur Seal, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Brown Fur Seals ( *Enhydra lutris*). The algorithm leverages the seal's efficient exploration of its environment, its tendency to cluster around promising areas, and its adaptation to changing environmental conditions to develop a robust and effective search strategy. Brown Fur Seal combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a novel adaptation mechanism based on the seal's observed foraging patterns. Specifically, the algorithm employs a dynamic population size adjustment, a polarization mechanism mimicking the seals' clustering behavior, and a mutation strategy inspired by their exploration of new feeding grounds. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its ability to converge to near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. The key contributions of this work include a novel algorithm design, a clear explanation of the underlying biological inspiration, and empirical validation through comparative analysis with established metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for various optimization challenges.

title: Quantum Privacy Computation Algorithm Based on Quantum Coherence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum privacy computation algorithm leveraging the principles of quantum coherence. The core claim is to design an algorithm capable of safeguarding data privacy within quantum computing environments. The central mechanism employs the phenomenon of quantum coherence to minimize the impact of sensitive data during computation, while simultaneously ensuring the accuracy of the resulting output. Unlike existing privacy-preserving techniques that rely on classical computation, this approach addresses the unique challenges presented by quantum computing. The algorithm focuses on strategically manipulating quantum states to obscure intermediate results and prevent adversaries from reconstructing the original data. Mathematical formulations are presented to illustrate the key components of the algorithm, including state preparation, quantum operations, and measurement procedures. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving privacy protection. This work represents a significant step towards practical quantum privacy computation.

title: 基于自组织网络的量子纠缠测量
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum entanglement measurement system based on a dynamically organized network of qubits. Traditional approaches rely on predefined measurement protocols, limiting precision. We propose a system where the quantum state is influenced by the network's dynamic evolution, allowing for more accurate and nuanced measurement outcomes. This system leverages the inherent properties of self-organization to achieve enhanced data fidelity. The core mechanism centers around constructing a quantum entanglement state within a dynamically adjusted network, resulting in improved signal processing and ultimately, more precise quantum information extraction. This research explores the potential of utilizing self-organization to overcome limitations in current quantum entanglement measurement techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Modeling: A Novel Tensor Analysis Framework
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents unique challenges and opportunities for information processing. This paper proposes a novel tensor analysis framework predicated on quantum entanglement, incorporating specific tensor operations designed to precisely capture the intricacies of this correlation. The core claim is that this framework enables more efficient and robust quantum computation through the strategic application of entanglement-based computations and a newly designed tensor operation. The mechanism involves leveraging quantum entanglement to store and manipulate information, offering a potential paradigm shift in quantum information processing. This work explores the theoretical foundations and potential implementation of this approach, demonstrating its capacity to address limitations of traditional tensor analysis methods.

title: A self-contained solver for magma law implications, with kernel-checked certificates
abstract: We describe a solver for implications between equational laws of magmas, built for Stage 2 of the SAIR competition. Each answer is a Lean 4 certificate checked by the organizer’s kernel: either a finite magma satisfying the hypothesis and violating the goal, or a proof of the implication. The solver is a single Python file of 108,748 bytes using only the standard library. It consults no database, embeds no lookup table, contains no problem-specific case, and makes no call to a language model. On a 200-problem sample set it settles all 200. The judge admits proofs whose axioms lie within propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; the proofs of implications here close over none of the three. Source, measurements and per-problem results are public under Apache-2.0.

title: Conditional Rewrite Rule Synthesis Using E-Graphs and Implication Propagation
abstract: Compilers, synthesizers, and theorem provers rely on rich rulesets for manipulating expressions via rewriting, but developing such rules remains difficult and error-prone. While prior work has automated synthesis of rewrite rules, it has focused largely on strict equalities, leaving conditional rewrites largely unsupported. Conditional rule synthesis explores a much larger search space because it must search for both the rule body and the condition. Effective pruning of the space is crucial for scaling synthesis to large grammars. The commonly used “derivability” metric for eliminating redundant rules in the strict setting does not extend directly to the conditional case. A conditional rule may be redundant not only when its body and condition are equivalent to a rule, but also when its condition implies a condition of a more general rule. We present CHOMPY, a tool for synthesizing conditional rewrite rules. CHOMPY’s core contribution is implication propagation, a technique that lifts equality saturation to the predicate level to discover logical implications between conditions, then uses those implications to obtain a new notion of conditional derivability and ruleset minimization. To evaluate CHOMPY, we compare the synthesized conditional ruleset to handwritten ones from Caviar (an equality saturation theorem prover) and Halide’s term rewriting system. CHOMPY’s rewrites derive 73.3% of Caviar’s and 57.1% of Halide’s conditional rules. CHOMPY outperforms an LLM-only baseline on both benchmarks. Unlike the LLM’s substantially variable output across runs, CHOMPY’s results are deterministic and stable.

title: Parallelizing Congruence Closure
abstract: Given a set of ground equalities over terms with uninterpreted function symbols, congruence closure computes the smallest equivalence relation containing these equalities that respects functional congruence. While congruence closure is a performance-critical component of SAT solvers, satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solvers, and equality saturation engines, all existing implementations are sequential. In this work, we provide the first parallel algorithms for congruence closure. We build on two ideas from the parallel algorithms literature: a union-find data structure that supports concurrent union operations and a semisort (group-by) algorithm that allows us to discover new congruences in parallel. We present two algorithms that replace the classic sequential worklist with a bulk-synchronous closure loop: each round processes all pending unions in parallel, detects new congruences, and repeats until a fixpoint. The two algorithms differ in how they identify which terms to re-examine in each round. We evaluate both these algorithms against a sequential baseline on a number of benchmarks and show near-linear speedup on up to 32 cores.

title: Exploring cause-effect relationships for trustworthy language-based maintenance chatbots
abstract: Diese Arbeit untersucht die Wirksamkeit der Erweiterung von auf Large Language Models (LLMs) basierenden Wartungs-Chatbots durch Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), das sowohl Vector Similarity Search (VSS) zur semantischen Informationsabfrage als auch Knowledge Graphs (KGs) zur strukturierten Wissensrepräsentation einbindet. Ziel ist es, die Leistung eines reinen LLM-Baseline-Modells mit zwei erweiterten Varianten zu vergleichen: einem LLM, das mittels VSS um externe Wissensquellen ergänzt wird, und einem LLM, das zusätzlich durch KGs unterstützt wird, die kausale Beziehungen explizit modellieren. Die Forschung adressiert insbesondere die Frage, in welchem Ausmaß die Integration von VSS-basiertem RAG sowie kausaler KI über KGs die Effektivität und Qualität der Problemlösung für Instandhaltungstechniker steigern kann - ein Aspekt, der in bisherigen vergleichenden Studien weitgehend fehlte.Die Untersuchung folgt einer zweigleisigen Methodik: einem systematischen Literaturreview und einer strukturierten Simulationsstudie. Das Literaturreview wurde gemäß PRISMA-Richtlinien durchgeführt und bündelte bestehende Erkenntnisse zur Kombination von LLMs, RAG (mit Fokus auf VSS) und KGs im Wartungsumfeld. Sechzehn wissenschaftliche Arbeiten wurden in das qualitative Review aufgenommen, wodurch eine theoretische Grundlage geschaffen.Die anschließende Simulationsstudie implementierte ein vergleichendes experimentelles Design unter Einsatz eines Chatbots auf Basis von GPT-4o und dem LangChain-Framework. Getestet wurden drei Konfigurationen: ein reines LLM (Baseline), ein mittels RAG erweitertes LLM (unter Nutzung historischer Wartungsprotokolle und Betriebsanweisungen via VSS), sowie ein KG-erweitertes LLM (unter Nutzung eines Neo4J-KGs, in dem kausale Relationen zwischen Symptomen, Wahrnehmungen und Fehlern explizit hinterlegt sind). Ein Katalog aus 120 Fragen - verteilt auf vier realitätsnahe Wartungsszenarien - simulierte typische initiale Diagnoseanfragen von Technikern. Jede Frage wurde in allen drei Konfigurationen beantwortet, woraus insgesamt 360 Antworten resultierten. Zwei unabhängige technische Experten, die keine Kenntnis darüber hatten, welche Modellvariante ihnen jeweils vorlag, bewerteten die Antworten hinsichtlich Vollständigkeit, Korrektheit und Konsistenz auf einer 5-Punkte-Likert-Skala.Die erwarteten Ergebnisse leiten sich aus der vergleichenden Analyse der Antwortqualität ab. Es wird davon ausgegangen, dass KG-erweiterte LLMs sowohl die Baseline als auch das ausschließlich durch VSS-basiertes RAG erweiterte Modell insbesondere hinsichtlich diagnostischer Korrektheit und Konsistenz übertreffen. Der Vorteil ergibt sich daraus, dass KGs kausale Zusammenhänge explizit repräsentieren und inferieren können - ein entscheidender Faktor für komplexe Fehlerdiagnosen - während RAG über VSS primär semantisch ähnliche Informationspassagen abruft, jedoch keine systematische kausale Struktur bereitstellt.Die Integration von KGs dürfte folglich die Fähigkeit des Chatbots signifikant stärken, kausale Erklärungen abzuleiten und Empfehlungen für nicht unmittelbar offensichtliche Geräteausfälle zu formulieren. Damit bietet die Arbeit eine empirische Grundlage für den Einsatz hybrider symbolisch-neuronaler Architekturen (LLM + KG) als besonders effektive, vertrauenswürdige und kausal bewusste KI-Assistenten in der industriellen Instandhaltung.

title: Misoginia en la conversación mediática digital: severidad, engagement y redes de interacción en X
abstract: Propósito: Analizar la presencia, intensidad y dinámica relacional del odio misógino en X en torno a contenidos de cinco medios informativos españoles. Metodología: Se recopilaron mensajes públicos de enero de 2021 a junio de 2022 mediante API y rutinas de automatización. Un sistema supervisado de clasificación permitió el cribado inicial y los mensajes candidatos fueron validados mediante etiquetado humano. La muestra final incluye 346 mensajes con contenido misógino o potencialmente misógino, codificados por tipo de odio asociado y por una escala ordinal de intensidad (0–5). Se evaluó el engagement (respuestas, retuits y “Me gusta”) y se construyó una red dirigida de interacción (Gephi) para caracterizar nodos y conexiones. Resultados: Predomina la misoginia general (85,3%) y la intensidad nivel 3 (275/346; 79,5%). El conjunto generó 41 respuestas, 35 retuits y 841 “Me gusta”, concentrándose en el nivel 3 el 85,4% de las respuestas, el 88,6% de los retuits y el 83,4% de los “Me gusta”. La red (333 nodos; 579 aristas) presenta conectividad baja (grado medio 1,739; clustering 0) y una intermediación media reducida (betweenness 2,04), con un grupo acotado de cuentas estructuralmente relevantes. Conclusiones: La misoginia aparece como hostilidad frecuente, pero de conversación limitada, sostenida por micro grupos y usuarios con capacidad de puente. Aportación original: Este estudio integra severidad del odio, métricas de interacción y estructura de red en un contexto vinculado a la prensa digital española, aportando evidencia útil para comprender la circulación de las narrativas misóginas y orientar estrategias de mitigación y contrarréplica proporcionales

title: PromptRefine: source-free unsupervised domain adaptation for remote sensing image classification via CLIP filtering
abstract: Despite the success of deep learning in remote sensing (RS) image classification, substantial domain shifts—stemming from heterogeneous sensors and diverse environmental conditions—frequently compromise model reliability. Although source-free unsupervised domain adaptation (SFUDA) has emerged as a critical paradigm to bypass data privacy and storage constraints, existing methods remain fragile in complex RS scenes where noisy pseudo-labels often trigger catastrophic semantic drift. We propose PromptRefine, a white-box SFUDA framework designed to anchor target adaptation through cross-modal intelligence. Specifically, we leverage the zero-shot semantic priors of large-scale vision–language models (e.g., contrastive language–image pre-training) to rectify source-biased predictions via a dynamic prompt fine-tuning mechanism. The framework executes a three-stage alternating optimization strategy that integrates cross-modal semantic alignment, hard-sample mining via sliced Wasserstein discrepancy, and fine-grained prompt evolution. Evaluated across 18 cross-domain tasks on five benchmarks (UCM, WHU-RS19, AID, RSSCN7, and NWPU-RESISC45), PromptRefine consistently achieves remarkable performance. Specifically, it outperforms the leading vision transformer-based baseline (VisTA) by 0.42% and 0.47% on the two groups of cross-domain tasks and surpasses the top ResNet-based baseline (SRKT/DFENet) by 2.94% and 5.02% in average classification accuracy. The proposed method also outperforms other SFUDA and unsupervised domain adaptation methods on all 18 tasks, demonstrating its superior adaptation capability. Our approach provides a robust, privacy-preserving, and computationally efficient solution, setting a benchmark for scalable RS scene characterization.

title: Testing Transferability of a Mortality Risk Model for Interhospital Transfer Using Real-World Electronic Health Records: External Validation and Model Enhancement
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mortality risk is often uncertain at the time of interhospital transfer (IHT). OBJECTIVES: We examined what happens when a published machine learning model for post-transfer mortality, SafeNET, is deployed in an independent health system with substantial data fragmentation and missingness and assessed the extent to which local model development can compensate for cross-system data limitations. DERIVATION COHORT: SafeNET was evaluated from published specifications using its original 14-variable feature schema and applied without modification. Locally trained gradient-boosting models (Categorical Boosting [CatBoost], Light Gradient Boosting, Extreme Gradient Boosting) were developed using a stratified 70/30 train-test split with five-fold cross-validation, class weighting, and random under-sampling to address class imbalance (~1:27). VALIDATION COHORT: We included 14,728 adult patients (≥ 18 yr) undergoing IHT at a multihospital academic health system from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2023. Functional status variables were missing in 85% of encounters, limiting direct implementation of the original feature set. PREDICTION MODEL: Discrimination, classification metrics (precision, recall, F1 score), and calibration (Brier score) were compared across SafeNET and locally trained models on the held-out test set. RESULTS: SafeNET achieved performance that closely approximated its development-site results (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC-ROC], 0.87; F1, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.69-0.77), indicating strong external consistency. Locally trained CatBoost models outperformed SafeNET (AUC-ROC, 0.92; F1, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.72-0.78) and demonstrated improved calibration (Brier 0.04 vs. 0.055). Key variables, including functional status, were missing in 85% of encounters, limiting direct implementation of the original feature set. Although recall exceeded 0.70 across most models, precision remained below 080 for several configurations, indicating important trade-offs relevant to clinical deployment. CONCLUSIONS: SafeNET's performance was reproducible in an external health system, supporting its portability. However, local models trained on system-specific electronic health record patterns achieved markedly higher accuracy and calibration. Real-world replication revealed major data-availability barriers and highlighted the tension between acceptable recall and suboptimal precision in critical-care prognostic applications.

title: Quantum steering detection of two-qubit states via Kolmogorov–Arnold networks with measurement and feature reduction
abstract: Abstract Quantum steering is an important form of nonclassical correlation and plays a central role in one-sided device-independent quantum information processing. However, efficiently determining whether an arbitrary two-qubit state is steerable remains challenging, since semidefinite-programming-based certification generally depends on the choice of measurement settings and can become computationally demanding. In this work, we propose an interpretable quantum steering detection scheme based on Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs). The training labels are generated through semidefinite programming for randomly sampled two-qubit density matrices. Several physically motivated feature representations are constructed to investigate the influence of measurement and feature reduction. Owing to their learnable univariate edge functions and symbolic formula extraction capability, KANs provide not only accurate classification but also a more transparent representation of the learned steering decision boundary. Numerical experiments show that the proposed KAN-based classifiers can distinguish states with SDP-detected steering from states for which no witness is found under the sampled measurements. title: Thinking-enhanced LoRA finetuning large language models for gas pipeline leak resolution
abstract: Given the frequency of gas pipeline leaks due to aging and corrosion, robust emergency response plans are critical. Currently, such plans are predominantly static and lack structured knowledge, which limits their utility in supporting rapid decision-making and providing real-time professional guidance. To address this issue, this paper proposes a fine-tuned large language model for gas pipeline leak resolution (LLM4GPL). Specifically, to instantiate the Thinking-enhanced framework, we constructed a domain-specific dataset based on gas pipeline leak emergency plans. We employed data distillation techniques to generate QA pairs embedded with explicit reasoning steps (Chain-of-Thought), rather than simple fact-retrieval pairs. Subsequently, we utilized the Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) strategy to fine-tune a Large Language Model (LLM). In this process, we specifically injected trainable low-rank matrices into the model’s Attention mechanisms and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) modules. This design enables the LLM to capture both the specialized knowledge and the multi-step cognitive logic required for emergency resolution. On the self-built dataset, the fine-tuned model attains the highest reported BLEU and ROUGE-L scores and the lowest test loss and perplexity among the evaluated configurations. An independent evaluation by three domain experts on 50 stratified test cases indicated higher plan quality for the proposed model than for the compared baselines, and GPT-4o scores corresponded closely with the expert ratings. All 648 source records originate from a single municipal gas enterprise; the reported results therefore establish internal performance on one organizational dataset and do not demonstrate external generalization or system-level operational reliability.

title: A privacy-preserving framework for electronic prescription verification
abstract: Electronic prescription systems support efficient and auditable medication dispensing. During prescription verification, pharmacies need to establish prescriber authorization, legitimate credential possession, and compliance with validity constraints while limiting unnecessary disclosure of sensitive medical information. This creates a fundamental tension between verification requirements and data minimization. Conventional approaches typically rely on full-record presentation and public-key-based signatures bound to persistent identifiers. Although these mechanisms support authenticity and accountability, they can disclose more information than is required and enable cross-transaction linkage of patients and prescribers. Moreover, prescription-validity checks can depend on protected attributes, such as the expiry date, that should remain hidden during verification. This paper presents a privacy-preserving prescription verification framework that supports anonymous-yet-accountable healthcare-professional authorization, selective disclosure and an issuer-authenticated holder public-key reference through BBS+ prescription credentials, and privacy-preserving verification of a hidden expiry attribute. The framework defines a prescription presentation protocol through which a patient submits a BBS+ selective-disclosure presentation proof, an expiry commitment, and two Bulletproof range proofs to a pharmacy. To address the consistency gap that can arise from a naïve composition of credential and validity proofs, the protocol connects these components through a common expiry commitment. The canonical hash of this commitment is authenticated as an issuer-authenticated BBS+ credential attribute and treated as disclosed during presentation, while both range-proof commitments are derived from the same presented expiry commitment. The pharmacy independently verifies the commitment hash before verifying the range proofs. Under the stated assumptions, this construction mitigates cross-component substitution attacks. The framework is analyzed under an explicit threat model and trust assumptions, and its protocol-level message flow is examined through symbolic verification. A proof-of-concept implementation evaluates the computational and communication overhead of the cryptographic operations under synthetic workloads. The results quantify the cryptographic processing and presentation payload overhead across the evaluated configurations within the stated experimental scope.

title: Local Gaussian bounds on the non-destructive discrimination of two-mode squeezed states
abstract: Typical measurement setups in quantum systems are destructive, meaning that states are irretrievably altered after measurement. In this work, we analyse non-destructive discrimination of two two-mode squeezed vacuum states using local Gaussian measurements. We investigate a tradeoff relation between the success probability of discrimination and the fidelity of the resulting state with the initial state, and construct a protocol given by local Gaussian measurements, which is optimal within our numerically explored class. We also extend to the case where we allow for additional pre-shared entanglement, and show that this regime allows us to exceed the standard local Gaussian bound for the fidelity-success probability tradeoff. Our work provides a natural extension of the tradeoff between information gain and disturbance in entangled-state discrimination, previously established for finite-dimensional quantum systems, to infinite-dimensional continuous-variable systems.

title: VATO: A Vortex-Force-Aware Transformer Operator for Unsteady Separated Aerofoil Flows
abstract: Accurate prediction of unsteady separated flows is challenging because the aerodynamic loads depend on nonlinear separation and vortex-shedding dynamics. Although high-fidelity CFD resolves these mechanisms, its cost limits repeated use in design and control. Standard field-level surrogate training, however, does not distinguish the flow regions that contribute most strongly to the aerodynamic loads. We introduce VATO (Vortex-Force-Aware Transformer Operator), which couples the Vortex Force Map (VFM) method to a geometry-aware neural operator through two complementary mechanisms. VATO-S adds training-only supervision of the local VFM force-contribution field, with no increase in model size or inference cost. VATO-A uses VFM contribution and sensitivity fields to prioritise force-relevant source locations for residual cross attention. The methods are evaluated on unsteady CFD data for double-edged-plate aerofoils over 54 trajectories from nine geometries. Over lead times of 1-20~ms, VATO-S reduces velocity, pressure, and vorticity errors by 10.4\%, 1.0\%, and 15.6\%, respectively, while VATO-A achieves reductions of 15.8\%, 7.5\%, and 31.2\%. VATO-S gives the lowest VFM-derived drag error, whereas VATO-A gives the lowest pressure-derived lift and drag errors. Over lead times extending 50\% beyond the training range, VATO-A retains a 26.9\% reduction in vorticity error and larger improvements in all four force readouts, despite reduced gains in velocity and pressure. These results show that force-aware operator learning can improve both flow-field prediction and aerodynamic functional accuracy in unsteady separated flows.

title: Adversarial Attacks as a Diagnostic Tool for a Mining Detection Network in the Brazilian Legal Amazon
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) applied to satellite imagery are increasingly adopted as the standard tool to detect mining in the Brazilian Legal Amazon, as their predicition start to feed environmental enforcement pipelines. We trained such a CNN and obtained an F1-Score of 0.9247 with an AUC of 0.9930. Adversarial attacks show that these numbers hide what the model learned. With the addition of random noise in the data, up to 45% of the of forest patches were missclassified as mining, while low-pass noise with the same budget and the same mean shift turns 0.5%, so the decision rests on high frequency texture. The fragility is asymmetric, since one FGSM step at 4/255 converts every forest patch into mining but evades only 5% of the real mining.

title: Old Search Trees, New Fruits: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of planning and search algorithms as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: ## Cape Gray Mongoose Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Cape Gray Mongoose Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CGMIMA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Cape Gray Mongoose (Urvafulrufus). The algorithm leverages the mongoose's strategic movement patterns, territory defense, and adaptive resource allocation strategies to develop a robust and efficient optimization method. CGMIMA incorporates key features such as a dynamic territory assignment mechanism, an adaptive exploration-exploitation balance, and a novel conflict resolution strategy inspired by the mongoose's social interactions. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a self-organized structure, mimicking the mongoose's group dynamics. The performance of CGMIMA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's core mechanism is represented by the following equations: * Position Update: $x_{i}^{k+1} = x_i^k + \alpha_{i}^{k} * rand(0,1) * (x_best^k - x_i^k) + \beta_{i}^{k} * (y_best^k - y_i^k)$ * Territory Assignment: $T(i) = argmax_{j \neq i} |x_i^k - x_j^k|$ where $T(i)$ represents the territory assigned to individual *i*. * Exploration-Exploitation Balance: $\alpha_{i}^{k} = sigmoid(\gamma_{k} * (y_i^k - y_best^k))$ * Conflict Resolution: $Conflict(i,j) = |x_i^k - x_j^k|$; $Resolution(i,j) = \eta * (1 - Conflict(i,j)) * rand(0,1)$ The algorithm's ability to adapt to changing landscapes and efficiently converge towards optimal solutions makes it a promising approach for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: Quantum Entanglement Regularization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. However, harnessing its full power is hampered by the inherent challenges of maintaining entanglement, controlling its properties, and effectively utilizing its non-local nature. This paper explores a novel regularization algorithm based on quantum entanglement, aiming to overcome these limitations and unlock new capabilities in quantum computing, specifically addressing the complexities of non-locality. We propose a mechanism that utilizes a '纠缠关联度矩阵' to establish constraints on entangled states, thereby enhancing computational efficiency and stability. This algorithm represents a significant step towards realizing a more robust and versatile quantum computing framework.

title: ##混沌几何的非线性优化算法
abstract: 混沌几何是自然界中复杂性和自组织性现象的数学模型,其特征在于局部最优解与全局最优解之间的差异。本研究致力于设计一种基于混沌几何的非线性优化算法,旨在利用混沌系统的自组织特性,在优化问题中寻找更有效的全局最优解,并探索其在优化领域的应用。本文提出了一种新的优化算法,该算法借鉴了混沌系统的自组织行为,并将其应用于优化问题的求解。该算法的核心机制是通过将混沌系统的自组织特性融入优化算法,模拟混沌系统的行为,从而寻找全局最优解,并避免了传统优化算法的局限性。通过对混沌几何的分析,我们深入探讨了其在优化领域中的潜在应用。

title: # Bucharian Vole-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the Bucharian Vole-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BVIOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bucharian vole. The Bucharian vole is known for its efficient and adaptable foraging strategies in complex environments. The BVIOA algorithm leverages key aspects of this behavior, including exploration, exploitation, and path planning, to develop a robust optimization approach. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism based on the vole's responsiveness to environmental changes. The core of the algorithm relies on a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, where particles represent potential solutions, and their movement is governed by a dynamically adjusted velocity vector. Specifically, the velocity update equation is modified to incorporate a "vole-inspired" exploration term, simulating the vole's tendency to deviate from established paths in search of better resources. Furthermore, a local search mechanism mimicking the vole's meticulous examination of discovered food sources is integrated to enhance exploitation capabilities. The performance of BVIOA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high solution quality and convergence speed compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, such as PSO and Genetic Algorithm. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for solving complex optimization problems across diverse fields.

title: ## Brown Spiny Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Brown Spiny Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BSMMA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the brown spiny mouse (*Acomys subspinosus*). These mice exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in challenging environments. The BSMMA algorithm leverages this behavior by mimicking the mouse's exploration and exploitation strategies. The core mechanism involves a population of agents, each representing a potential solution. These agents move through the search space, influenced by both global and local information, mirroring the spiny mouse's reliance on both collective knowledge and individual observations. The algorithm utilizes a novel distance metric based on a modified Euclidean distance, incorporating a stochastic element to simulate the unpredictable terrain encountered by the mice. The algorithm's parameters – exploration rate (ε) and exploitation rate (α) – are dynamically adjusted based on the perceived density of food sources, analogous to the spiny mouse's adaptation to environmental changes. This paper presents the algorithm's theoretical framework, its implementation details, and demonstrates its effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems. The results demonstrate that the BSMMA algorithm achieves competitive performance compared to existing metaheuristic algorithms like the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO).

title: Title: Deterministic Quantum Simulation of Non-Equilibrium Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel deterministic quantum simulation method designed to accurately model complex non-equilibrium systems, offering a significant advancement over existing approaches. The core claim is the creation of a technique capable of simulating these systems with a guaranteed level of fidelity, facilitating a deeper understanding of their dynamics. This method leverages a time-evolving simulation, dynamically adjusting simulation parameters based on the system's state, addressing a major limitation in current quantum simulation – stability challenges. The research explores and validates the effectiveness of this technique through a series of simulations of various non-equilibrium systems, demonstrating improved accuracy and robustness compared to traditional methods. We provide a detailed explanation of the core mechanism and discuss the potential implications for various scientific disciplines.
