title: ## Budin's Chinchilla Rat: A Meta-Heuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Rodent Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a novel meta-heuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Budin's Chinchilla Rat" (BCR), inspired by the foraging behavior of chinchillas, specifically drawing upon observations of their efficient path planning and resource acquisition strategies. BCR leverages a combination of local search techniques, a simulated annealing process mimicking the chinchilla's thermoregulation, and a dynamic population management system influenced by the rodent's territoriality. The algorithm aims to achieve robust performance across a range of optimization problems, particularly those involving discrete and continuous variables. The core of BCR lies in its adaptive parameter tuning, driven by a self-learning mechanism that adjusts the influence of each component based on observed performance. We demonstrate BCR's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its potential as a competitive meta-heuristic. The algorithm's key characteristics include a reduced computational complexity compared to some established meta-heuristics and a demonstrated ability to escape local optima effectively. Future work will explore the algorithm's application in diverse fields and its integration with machine learning techniques.

title: Brown Howler Monkey: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Vocalizations of the Howler Monkey
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Brown Howler Monkey" (BHM), inspired by the complex and dynamic vocalizations of the brown howler monkey ( *Alouatta involucrata* ). The algorithm leverages the principles of competitive social behavior, territorial defense, and call pattern modulation observed in these primates to establish a robust search strategy for solving complex optimization problems. BHM employs a population-based approach with a unique adaptation mechanism mimicking howler monkey calls – a "modulation pulse" – to dynamically adjust the exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm's core components include a population initialization, a fitness evaluation function, a modulation pulse generation process, and a selection and replacement mechanism. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's convergence properties and its potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods, particularly in scenarios with discontinuous objective functions and complex landscapes. Performance evaluations on a range of benchmark optimization problems showcase BHM's competitiveness against established algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The key innovations of BHM lie in its adaptive modulation pulse and its ability to effectively manage the trade-off between exploration and exploitation.

title: Brazilian Big-Eyed Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bat-Inspired Adaptive Search (BIAS)," inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian big-eyed bat ( *Pteropedes brasilianus*). These bats exhibit a unique aerial hunting strategy characterized by rapid dives, precise adjustments based on echo location, and a collective search pattern. BIAS leverages these characteristics to develop an optimization algorithm suitable for tackling complex, non-linear optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of bat behavior, including an intrinsic motivation parameter (representing the bat's desire to search), an extrinsic motivation parameter (reflecting the attractiveness of potential solutions), and an adaptive adjustment mechanism mimicking the bats' directional adjustments during flight. Mathematical formulations describing the core components of BIAS, including the intrinsic and extrinsic motivation functions, and the adaptive adjustment mechanism, are presented. The algorithm's convergence properties are discussed, and preliminary simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness in solving benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its potential as a robust and efficient metaheuristic approach. The algorithm's performance is evaluated based on metrics such as solution accuracy, convergence speed, and computational complexity.

title: Borneo Black-banded Squirrel-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Borneo Black-banded Squirrel Algorithm (BBSA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Borneo Black-banded Squirrel (Ratufa indica). These squirrels exhibit a unique strategy of exploring and exploiting resources within a defined area, characterized by a 'black band' – an area of high resource concentration. The BBSA algorithm mimics this behavior through a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, incorporating a novel 'black band' identification mechanism and a modified particle movement strategy. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing particles representing potential solutions. Each particle's position in the search space is updated based on a combination of global and local search information, guided by the identified 'black band' areas. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of the search space based on resource density, mirroring the squirrel's efficient resource utilization. The algorithm's parameters, including the 'black band' threshold and the exploration/exploitation ratio, are carefully tuned to achieve optimal performance. The results indicate that the BBSA algorithm offers a competitive alternative to existing metaheuristic methods, particularly for problems exhibiting clustered or spatially correlated solutions. The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising tool for various complex optimization challenges.

title: Bornean Mountain Ground Squirrel-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bornean Mountain Ground Squirrel (BMGS) Algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bornean Mountain Ground Squirrel (Spermophilus everetti). These rodents exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in complex, mountainous terrain. The algorithm leverages this behavior through a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies, mimicking the squirrel's movement patterns and decision-making process. Specifically, the BMGS algorithm employs a multi-dimensional search space, utilizing a population of agents, each representing a potential solution. Movement within this space is guided by a stochastic function based on the squirrel's navigation strategy, incorporating elements of random exploration and local optimization. The algorithm's core components include a mutation operator mimicking the squirrel's exploratory movements and a selection mechanism based on the perceived food availability (fitness). The performance of the BMGS algorithm is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's key characteristics are its adaptability to diverse problem landscapes and its potential for efficient convergence. The results indicate that the BMGS algorithm offers a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems exhibiting complex, multi-modal landscapes. Further research will explore the algorithm's parameter sensitivity and its application to more challenging real-world optimization problems.

title: Blue Nile Patas Monkey: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Social Dynamics
abstract: This paper presents Blue Nile Patas Monkey (BNPM), a newly developed metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the social dynamics observed in Blue Nile Patas monkeys ( *Papio bernardinelli*). BNPM leverages the principles of information sharing, dominance hierarchies, and coalition formation within monkey groups to establish a robust and efficient search strategy for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key features such as a dynamic population size, adaptive inertia weights, and a novel convergence criterion based on the concept of "social influence." We demonstrate the effectiveness of BNPM through simulations on a range of benchmark problems, including the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP), the Rastrigin Function, and the Sphere Function. The results show that BNPM consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging and high-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm's adaptability and ability to handle diverse problem landscapes are attributed to its biomimetic approach, drawing inspiration from the intricate social structures of these fascinating primates. The core of BNPM lies in the 'social influence' metric which determines the contribution of each individual in the population to the overall solution exploration. This metric is dynamically adjusted based on the individual's performance and its perceived influence on other members of the population.

title: Geometric Chaos in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the phenomenon of geometric chaos within neural network activations, exploring its potential impact on network stability and interpretability. We propose a novel method for quantifying and controlling this chaos, leveraging network geometric structure analysis to identify and mitigate instability. The core mechanism centers on identifying and manipulating patterns within the network's correlations to achieve a more ordered and predictable activation landscape. The research aims to contribute to a deeper understanding of neural network behavior and potentially unlock new avenues for AI design.

title: Hardware-Enforced Physical Interlock Architecture for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Equipment
abstract: This is a defensive publication establishing public prior art for a hardware-enforced physical interlock architecture for nucleic acid synthesis equipment. A fixed-function hardware gate is positioned on one or more critical physical paths required to initiate, continue, complete, or release the product of a synthesis cycle, held disabled by hardware default and enabled only upon verification of a cryptographically signed, single-use attestation token from a separately provisioned hardware execution controller. This makes screening compliance a physical property of the synthesis machine itself, independent of and unreachable by the machine's own software, rather than a software policy that can be bypassed, disabled, or misconfigured. The author and publisher dedicate this specific invention to the public domain. No patent rights are sought or reserved for the subject matter described.

title: Beyond Smart Marketing
abstract: The emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has reshaped the tourism paradigm, moving from mere operational automation to the creation of hyper-personalised service ecosystems. However, current literature reveals a critical tension: as technical efficiency advances, significant gaps emerge around emotional engagement and ethical integrity. This chapter analyses the transition from “smart marketing” to the integration of emotional AI, evaluating how recommendation systems, affective chatbots, and immersive technologies influence tourist behaviour and destination sustainability. Through a comprehensive review of secondary sources, the study proposes adopting the “hetero-intelligence” framework, which combines the analytical capacity of algorithms with human contextual and ethical judgment. It concludes that, to ensure the long-term viability of the sector, it is imperative to balance technological innovation with principles of transparency, responsibility, and humanised design, thus mitigating the risks of bias and dehumanisation in the tourist experience.

title: A Data-Driven Two-Layer Case-Based Reasoning Framework for Intelligent Deep Excavation Retaining Structure Selection Under Incomplete Information
abstract: In early-stage projects, incomplete geological data can affect the selection of retaining structures for deep excavations. This paper proposes an adaptive two-layer Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) framework to address this issue. First, a case database was constructed; feature interaction terms were incorporated into the similarity measure to capture the nonlinear coupling among geological parameters, and a Gradient Boosted Decision Tree (GBDT) was employed to achieve an objective, data-driven allocation of feature weights. The first layer implements a gating mechanism based on logical conjunction and adaptive tolerance thresholds, which automatically switches between the two inference paths when information is missing, preventing invalid hard matches; the second layer applies K-means++ clustering and local inductive reasoning to mitigate the biases caused by data sparsity. Experiments demonstrate that, under conditions of parameter incompleteness and noise interference, the method’s Top-3 recommendation accuracy significantly outperforms traditional models and machine learning baseline models and exhibits strong resistance to interference, providing a solid methodological foundation for retaining structure selection in complex data scenarios.

Experiments demonstrate that, under conditions of parameter incompleteness and noise interference, the method’s Top-3 recommendation accuracy significantly outperforms traditional models and machine learning baseline models and exhibits strong resistance to interference, providing a solid methodological foundation for retaining structure selection in complex data scenarios.

title: A Grounding-Theoretic Refinement of the BFO Standard Realizables Classification
abstract: Realizable entities are modal properties that are realized in processes. In the top-level ontology Basic Formal Ontology (BFO), realizable entities are classified by appeal to internal and external groundedness: dispositions and functions are internally grounded, whereas roles are externally grounded. This paper introduces a meta-ontology of grounding for refining the BFO notions of groundedness. In particular, it proposes to re-characterize internal groundedness in terms of partial immediate categorical grounding. This proposed refinement resolves a function-grounding challenge facing the BFO standard realizables classification while requiring only modest adjustments to BFO. It also accommodates apparently extrinsic dispositions and physically grounded roles.

title: Channel attention of the image for distinguishing ductal carcinoma in situ from benign mimics based on ultrasound images
abstract: Background: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is widely recognized as a precursor to invasive breast cancer, with an estimated 20-50% of cases progressing to invasive disease. The early detection of DCIS could save doctors and patients more time to deal with the breast cancer, which has posed a great threat to the life safety of women worldwide. This study aimed to develop a deep learning algorithm based on the image-level attention to distinguish DCIS from the benign mimics on ultrasound images, assisting doctors in screening for benign breast lesions. Methods: By screening the biopsy results of 3,327 patients, the ultrasound images of 612 patients were retrospectively collected, including DCIS and benign mimics. The dataset was randomly split at the patient level into training (70%, n=430) and test (30%, n=182) sets. Using ResNet18 as the backbone architecture, we compared and developed models with image-level attention mechanisms. Model performance was evaluated on the test set using the area under the curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. To assess the statistical significance of performance differences between models, the Holm-Bonferroni correction was employed to account for multiple comparisons. Results: Through quantitative comparison with 6 shallow benchmark algorithms such as AlexNet, VGG16, GoogleNet, ResNet18, CoAtNet and Swin Transformer, the effectiveness of our method was demonstrated, which achieved the best performance with AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision and F1-score of 0.868±0.009, 0.835±0.016, 0.767±0.056, 0.916±0.057, 0.916±0.059, 0.835±0.04, respectively. After Holm-Bonferroni correction, these improvements were statistically significant (corrected P<0.05) compared to all other models. The effect size of AUC, specificity, precision, F1-score were 0.69, 0.68, 0.89, 0.58, respectively, revealing large practical improvement. Furthermore, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (GradCAM) visualization confirmed that our model focused more accurately on lesion regions, providing interpretability for its superior feature extraction. Conclusions: In this paper, we proposed the ResNet18-CA for the classification of DCIS and confused cases, which was good at learning the ultrasound image features. The proposed network achieved higher accuracy than the other methods being compared.

title: Evaluación automática en robótica industrial mediante MATLAB Grader
abstract: This article analyzes the integration of MATLAB Grader into the "Robot Control and Programming" course at the University of La Rioja, progressing from purely formative use in a laboratory setting to comprehensive course assessment. A formative and evaluative learning path was designed using this tool, consisting of exercises composed of fragmented tasks with increasing difficulty, limited attempts, self-assessment, and weighting. This path was implemented during the 2025-2026 academic year. The quantitative results obtained (22 students assessed) are analyzed, correlating progress during the automated practical exercises with performance observed in traditional final exams, both regular and resit. The data reveal that the technical rigor of the automated assessment acts as a harsh filter, leading to critical dropout rates, especially in advanced modules. This raises a crucial debate about current student persistence and how to approach assessment using scripts in groups of students in courses related to control, automation, and robotics.

title: Metatheoretical multiverse analysis: Improving the reliability of research with theories-as-data
abstract: Here we present a method for measuring, analyzing and reducing theoretical uncertainty. We call it metatheoretical multiverse analysis (MMA). The method is important because the reliability and replicability of scientific observation and testing of a phenomenon are a function of theoretical uncertainty thus reducing it is a method for improving theory. The MMA method requires encoding theory as propositional logic between variables (nodes) and their relationships with one another (edges). Propositional logic models are treated as causal path models in our method, which enable mathematical properties of testing and identification underlying their causal propositions. By encoding theories-as-data including their unknown components, it is possible to generate a multiverse of alternatively plausible theoretical models which can then be meta-analyzed using techniques borrowed from (statistical) multiverse analysis. We introduce metrics for studying theoretical multiverses that enable measuring and identifying the causes of metatheoretical uncertainty. This guides researchers to where it is best to invest theoretical development to reduce uncertainty. We use three simulations and a dedicated software package to demonstrate this method.

title: Zeta-Lite: A Concurrent, Branchable In-Browser SQL Database for Agentic Memory
abstract: The browser has become a first-class database host: applications increasingly want to store, query, and reason over structured data entirely on the client - for privacy, offline operation, local-first collaboration, and, most recently, as durable memory for in-browser AI agents. One way to get SQL in the browser, compiling PostgreSQL to WebAssembly (PGlite), inherits PostgreSQL's process model: a single backend connection that executes one statement at a time and blocks. That model cannot express concurrent transactions, and it leaves richer capabilities - graph queries, database branching - to whatever the compiled server happens to include. We present zeta-lite, the browser form factor of the Zeta database engine: a WebAssembly build that compiles the same Zeta server down to a 2.87 MB gzipped artifact. Zeta-lite keeps the engine's log-centric asynchronous MVCC core, which yields two capabilities no other in-browser SQL engine provides. First, overlapping snapshot-isolated transactions on a single thread: multiple transactions hold distinct read/commit timestamps and interleave, with snapshot-isolation conflict detection between them. Second, copy-on-write database branching - whole-database fork, merge, and rebase - is unique in a browser SQL database and rare even in servers. On top of these, zeta-lite exposes a feature-complete PostgreSQL surface (joins, CTEs, window functions, JSONB with GIN indexes, full-text search, HNSW vector search, SQL/PGQ graph queries, multi-database) and snapshot-to-OPFS durability. Across Chrome, Firefox, and a native reference runtime, zeta-lite sustains 268k-315k point reads/s and holds a mixed read/write workload flat over millions of operations. This small, fully-featured, concurrent SQL database is an especially good fit for agentic memory - where cheap branchable state lets an agent explore, inspect, and commit or discard speculative work.

title: Recent Developments in Transformer Inference Deployment on FPGA Platforms: A Survey
abstract: With the rapid and continuous growth in the incorporation of machine learning models based on the Transformer architecture, capable deployment is in high demand. In this context, capable deployment refers to operational performance aspects, e.g., throughput and latency, as well as efficiency aspects, e.g., energy consumption. When it comes to the task of inference using such models, purpose-built hardware accelerators provide a lucrative alternative to common deployment choices, such as Central Processing Units (CPUs) and Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). The Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) platforms category is an example of such alternative accelerators, promising implementation flexibility, energy efficiency, improved latency and suitability for on-site deployment. We investigate the most recent advances, trends, and design choices for Transformer inference on FPGA platforms. We perform a systematic literature review, extracting and delving into preferred techniques for implementation and optimisation. This study and the provided taxonomy of topics could act as a guide for researchers from the academia and industry alike.

title: CERF: Communication-Efficient and Retraining-Free Collaborative Perception
abstract: Collaborative perception shares information among multiple agents to obtain a comprehensive scene representation, enhancing the perceptual capability of individual agents. However, most existing methods rely on transmitting and fusing dense feature maps for collaboration, which incurs inevitable communication overhead and heterogeneity challenges, limiting their practicality for real-world deployment. To address these challenges, we propose CERF, a novel Communication-Efficient and Retraining-Free framework for open heterogeneous collaborative perception. In CERF, we introduce a new virtual modality (termed Poture), which is generated from the perception outputs of other agents, to augment the extracted Bird's Eye View (BEV) features of the ego agent. To mitigate transmission delays, we employ a Kalman-filter based tracker and a motion forecasting model to derive the current predictions from historical perception results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CERF achieves performance comparable to mainstream intermediate-collaboration methods while reducing communication overhead by 95% across various downstream tasks. Furthermore, CERF enables seamless integration of unknown heterogeneous agents into the existing collaborative framework without additional retraining costs. Code is available at https://github.com/uestchjw/CERF.

title: SOVER: Formal Certification of Optimization Reformulations via LLM-Assisted SMT Verification
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable promise in translating and reformulating complex mathematical optimization problems across modeling languages. However, validating such transformations through empirical solver executions alone is unreliable, as solver outcomes may be affected by local minima, structural timeouts, numerical artifacts, and subtle semantic divergence between formulations. We introduce SOVER, an LLM-assisted SMT framework that separates semantic mapping from formal certification: Z3 checks domain cross-feasibility and global objective-order preservation for mixed-integer linear formulations, while dReal provides tolerance-aware feasibility/range and $ε$-argmin checks for continuous nonlinear formulations. We also introduce NLEquiv-150, a public benchmark of 100 equivalent and 50 deliberately hard non-equivalent nonlinear reformulation pairs. With LLM-extracted mappings, SOVER classifies 149/150 pairs (99.33%) correctly, including all 50 hard negatives; the sole error is an incomplete mapping extraction.

title: Independent Reinforcement Learning in Discounted Markov Games
abstract: In this work, we study radically uncoupled learning in discounted general-sum Markov games. Assuming ``$\mathsf{ETH}$ for $\mathsf{PPAD}$", we show that, for every fixed discount factor, there is no polynomial-time algorithm for computing inverse-polynomially accurate coarse correlated equilibria in discounted general-sum Markov games when players learn independently in decentralized settings. Complementing this hardness result, we provide what appears to be the first \emph{radically uncoupled} algorithm with sub-exponential convergence guarantees to coarse correlated equilibria in discounted general-sum Markov games without imposing any structural restrictions on the game. Our algorithm is a \emph{layered} variant of optimistic mirror descent with an increasing step-size schedule tailored to the multi-agent setting. Finally, we develop both full-feedback and partial feedback versions of the aforementioned algorithm and establish sub-exponential convergence guarantees for each case.

title: Who Guards the Guard? Evaluating Deterministic, LLM-Based, and Hybrid Firewalls for Tool-Using Agents
abstract: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents process untrusted files, URLs, and tables at a boundary where data may be mistaken for instructions. This paper compares four interface-level conditions: no firewall, deterministic policy enforcement, an LLM-based Tool-Input Minimizer/Tool-Output Sanitizer, and a gated hybrid. The evaluation has two stages. The development microbenchmark contains 19 adversarial and 4 benign cases, 6 Groq-hosted guard backbones, 2 repetitions, and 1,104 executions. A second frozen-policy held-out study contains 42 unseen adversarial variants and 20 benign hard negatives. Its primary analysis uses four complete guard backbones, three repetitions for LLM-dependent conditions, and case-level aggregation. In the development set, the hybrid condition exhibited no successful attacks among 228 adversarial executions. This result did not generalize: on the held-out set, both the deterministic and hybrid conditions achieved a case-mean attack success rate (ASR) of 54.76%, because the hybrid router invoked the semantic guard in 0/744 executions. The LLMonly condition reached 50.60% case-mean ASR, 92.08% benign utility, and 33/744 structured-output failures under a fail-open policy. The results show that deterministic checks are suitable for explicit structural constraints, but composition alone is insufficient; hybrid security depends on routing coverage, guard availability, and evaluation against attacks not used in constructing the defense.

title: A Federated Learning Model for Privacy-Preserving and Personalized Mental Health Monitoring using Big Data Analytics
abstract: Mental health disorders are rising globally, posing challenges in early detection, personalized care, and data privacy. The conventional centralized Machine Learning (ML) models involve the transfer of sensitive patient information to central servers, a factor that jeopardizes privacy and reduces user confidence. In addition, these models normally do not consider individual differences in behavior and thus generalized predictions are made, which are less accurate. To address these shortcomings, this research proposed a Federated Learning (FL)-based model of mental health monitoring that allows training models without raw data sharing in distributed medical customers. The model incorporates the concept of Big Data Analytics (BDA) to handle heterogeneous mental health records and assist with user-level customization and meaningful evaluation based on overall performance measures. The simulation outcomes indicate that the proposed model has a global accuracy of 99.53% and a miss rate of just 0.47% which beats conventional centralized methods. This research highlights a scalable, secure, and personalized solution for mental healthcare, advancing the integration of federated learning and big data in digital health systems.

title: PartHackBench: Certified Equal-Progress Stress Tests for Partial-Credit Tool-Agent Evaluation
abstract: Long-horizon tool agents often make useful progress without reaching terminal success, motivating partial-credit evaluation. Yet evaluators may reward milestones that were temporary, later reversed, or not attributable to the evaluated agent. Comparing an honest trajectory with a higher-scoring adversarial one is inconclusive if the latter made more genuine progress. We introduce PartHackBench, a controlled methodology that removes this confound. A private certifier admits a pair only when its trajectories match component-wise in both current-state predicate satisfaction and standardized agent attribution; score inflation, ∆hack = f(A) − f(H), is measured only afterward. In 18 sealed held-out tasks in PB-CSTE, the frozen historical-target run produced matched adversaries for 15 tasks. Historical credit yielded mean inflation of .252, conditional attack success of 10/15, end-to-endyield of 10/18, and detected none of 14 strict rollbacks. Semantic LLM judges were more resistant but remained vulnerable, especially under evaluator-targeted attacks, while PB-CSTE current-state controls, defined as exact functions of the certified components, yielded zero inflation by construction. PartHackBench thus provides a certified control for testing whether evaluator credit changes while all benchmark-defined task-relevant progress remains fixed.

title: AHUM Technical Note - The Modular Class
abstract: The canonical matrix Phi of the AHUM (Algebraic Hypergraph Unification Model) program is a 13 x 137 binary parity-check matrix whose rows are defined by modular rules on the column indices: eight residue classes mod 15, three antipodal "twisted" pairs, one mod 5 class pair, and the all-ones row. We enumerate its modular class M exhaustively — all C(14,8) x C(7,3) = 105,105 matrices obtained by varying the residue and pair choices — and compute the spectral dimension d_spec of the bipartite Tanner graph of each element, with no sampling. The class is rigid (median d_spec = 3.75 versus 4.35 for density-matched random matrices) and its heavy right tail consists entirely of GF(2) rank-deficient elements. The canonical Phi lies at the 0.38th percentile of the full class and the 0.98th percentile of the rank-13 stratum. title: Spanda: Zero-Cost Lexical Entropy Matches Neural Semantic Uncertainty—Until Frontier Models Break It
abstract: Detecting hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) requires estimating uncertainty. Neural Semantic Entropy accurately detects hallucinations by clustering generated paths using an auxiliary Natural Language Inference (NLI) model, but incurs massive computational overhead. In this paper, we propose Spanda, introducing a zero-cost normalized lexical metric ($R_{sc}$). We empirically evaluate models across four scales (1.5B to 120B). We demonstrate that for mid-sized models (7B–27B), $R_{sc}$ achieves an AUROC of 0.889, matching neural semantic entropy without the NLI overhead. However, on frontier models (120B+), we discover that intense RLHF alignment induces 'Confident Mode Collapse'—the model hallucinates the exact same incorrect answer across all paths, causing AUROC to invert to 0.091 and bypassing self-consistency assumptions.

title: 基于量子纠缠的非线性拓扑几何学
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for non-linear topology based on quantum entanglement, aiming to provide a powerful tool for modeling and understanding complex systems. We propose a new quantum entanglement state and a corresponding topological algorithm that leverages the instantaneous correlations inherent in this state to simulate and manipulate the intricate structure of topological spaces. The core mechanism centers around the ability to leverage quantum entanglement to achieve algorithmic advancements beyond classical computation. This work explores the potential of this framework to unlock new computational paradigms and offers a potential foundation for future quantum computing advancements.

title: Cameroon Cusimanse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Cameroon Cusimanse
abstract: This paper presents Cameroon Cusimanse, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the behavior of the Cameroon Cusimanse, a fascinating primate known for its deliberate and strategic movements. The algorithm, termed CCusimanse, leverages a combination of principles observed in the Cusimanse's foraging and navigation strategies, including adaptive step sizes, a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism, and a dynamic population diversity maintenance technique. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, CCusimanse focuses on maintaining a diverse population while simultaneously adapting to the problem landscape. The core of the algorithm involves a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating a new velocity update rule and a dynamic inertia weight adjustment scheme. Theoretical analysis suggests that CCusimanse possesses characteristics conducive to both efficient exploration and exploitation of the search space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CCusimanse through a series of benchmark problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO, Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Simulated Annealing (SA). The results indicate that CCusimanse offers a promising approach to complex optimization challenges.

title: 基于几何拓扑的动态数据压缩算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic data compression algorithm based on geometric topology. Traditional compression methods often rely on manual design and limited adaptability. Our proposed algorithm leverages the inherent topological structure of data to dynamically adjust the data representation, resulting in significantly improved compression efficiency and enhanced data storage capabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments, showcasing substantial gains in compression ratios and storage utilization compared to existing techniques. The core mechanism centers around the application of quantum entanglement and geometric topology to restructure data, facilitating a more efficient and robust compression process.

title: Buka Island Melomys: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Melomys rubicola*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Buka Island Melomys" (BIM), inspired by the foraging strategies of the *Melomys rubicola* (Buka Island Melomys) population on Buka Island, Papua New Guinea. These melomys exhibit a unique and efficient foraging behavior characterized by a combination of exploration and exploitation, specifically utilizing a 'patch-based' search strategy and a dynamic adjustment of step sizes based on food availability. BIM leverages these observed behaviors to construct a new algorithm for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates a patch-based search mechanism, dynamically adjusting step sizes, and a novel convergence criterion based on patch coverage. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness on a range of benchmark optimization problems, highlighting its potential for tackling challenging optimization tasks. The algorithm's performance is compared with existing metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to illustrate its competitive capabilities. The core idea is to mimic the melomys' ability to efficiently navigate their environment and select food sources, translating this into an adaptive and robust optimization process. The algorithm aims to achieve high solution quality and computational efficiency.

title: Buenos Aires Leaf-Eared Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Buenos Aires Leaf-Eared Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BALIMHA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the *Peromyscus labilis* (Buenos Aires leaf-eared mouse). The algorithm leverages the mouse's adaptive movement strategy – specifically, its ability to navigate complex environments while optimizing for food acquisition – to generate a new optimization process. BALIMHA incorporates elements of exploration and exploitation, mimicking the mouse's dynamic adjustments to environmental changes and resource availability. The core of the algorithm centers on a modified particle representation where each particle's position reflects the mouse's movement path, and velocity is adjusted based on a simulated 'hearing' mechanism that prioritizes areas with higher potential rewards. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's key components, including the fitness function, the velocity update rule, and the probabilistic selection of candidate solutions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions within a reasonable timeframe. The results indicate BALIMHA's potential as a robust and efficient metaheuristic for a wide range of optimization problems.

title: ## Brazilian Shrew-mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Shrew-Mouse Optimization Algorithm (SMOA)," inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian shrew-mouse (Kerivoula brasiliensis). These rodents exhibit a unique strategy of searching for food resources in complex and uncertain environments. SMOA leverages this behavior through a combination of adaptive exploration and exploitation phases, utilizing a novel representation of the search space and an innovative mechanism for adjusting the algorithm's parameters based on environmental feedback. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, simulating the shrew-mouse's navigation and resource acquisition. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SMOA on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform existing metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. The core innovation lies in the algorithm's ability to dynamically adapt its search strategy to the characteristics of the problem landscape, mirroring the shrew-mouse's intelligent response to changing conditions. This research contributes a new perspective on metaheuristic design, drawing inspiration from natural behaviors to create a robust and adaptable optimization tool.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction (QCS)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum mechanics to revolutionize Constraint Satisfaction (CS) algorithms, aiming to overcome the limitations of classical approaches. The core claim is to develop a novel QCS algorithm that leverages quantum mechanics to significantly enhance the exploration of the constraint space, ultimately leading to more efficient and effective solutions. We will detail the proposed mechanism, highlighting the theoretical basis and potential advantages over existing methods. The paper presents a conceptual framework and outlines the challenges and future research directions in this area.

title: Title: Topological Phase Field Theory (TPFT)
abstract: This paper introduces Topological Phase Field Theory (TPFT), a novel approach to quantum computation that leverages the principles of topology to enhance stability and adaptability. Traditional quantum algorithms are limited by the inherent noise of the environment, requiring explicit manipulation of quantum states. TPFT overcomes this limitation by incorporating dynamic, topological structures that actively resist environmental disturbances, allowing for self-adaptive quantum state evolution. We present a framework for designing and implementing quantum circuits that exhibit enhanced robustness and can respond to changing environments. The core mechanism centers around constructing and manipulating topological phases within the quantum state, which provides a fundamentally different approach to quantum state management. This work explores the potential of TPFT to surpass the limitations of traditional quantum algorithms, particularly in applications requiring dynamic adaptation and robust operation.

This approach offers a fundamentally different approach to computational design, addressing limitations of traditional frameworks in complex problem-solving.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Robotic Planning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to robotic planning that integrates the strengths of neural networks and symbolic reasoning engines. Current robotic planning systems often falter when confronted with the complexities of real-world environments, necessitating a more sophisticated method capable of handling both perceptual data and abstract reasoning. Our system combines a neural network, trained for environmental feature extraction, with a symbolic planning engine. The neural network processes raw sensory input, identifying and extracting relevant features, which are then fed as input to the symbolic engine. This allows for the generation of plans based on learned perceptual understanding and logical planning capabilities. The core claim of this work is that this integrated approach offers a significantly more robust and flexible solution compared to traditional methods, addressing the limitations of purely neural or purely symbolic planning systems. This paper outlines the architecture, training methodology, and potential applications of this neuro-symbolic reasoning framework for robotic planning.

title: Self-Reports Are Not Verification
abstract: Language model agents increasingly propose actions, observe external feedback, and explain their own behavior. Their confidence and rationales are convenient oversight signals, but convenience is not verification. We introduce an environment-grounded audit in which every intermediate proposal receives an exact outcome. A language model operates an evolutionary Contexto search whosefeedback function assigns every valid guess an exact rank without human annotation. Across 200 runs spanning five configurations and three model families, four reporting configurations produce 12,249 self-reports. We test three assumptions: stated confidence is calibrated, inherited rationales affect later proposals, and outcome-based selection improves report quality. All three fail. Operators overstate top-100 success by factors of 4.8 to 9.3, while calibration and discrimination dissociate across model families. Controlled interventions on 754 inherited rationales bound any measured benefit of the genuine rationale to roughly 250 ranks. Neither fitness-based nor random selection produces a detectable selection differential or parent-to-offspring transmission in report accuracy, despite sharply different search behavior. Agent self-reports should therefore be treated as claims to verify against the environment, not as evidence of their own reliability. Lab: Machine Intelligence and Biocomputing Lab (MIB) at School of Computing Supervisor: Dr. Ting Hu Supporting lab supervisor: Ryan Zhou

title: Regional distributed photovoltaic power forecasting based on dynamic meteorological characteristics
abstract: The dispersed spatial distribution of distributed photovoltaic （DPV） systems makes existing coarse-grained meteorological data inadequate for capturing local weather variations caused by the geographical offsets of PV stations， thereby limiting forecasting accuracy. To address this issue， this paper proposes a regional DPV power forecasting model based on fine-grained solar irradiance identification and a dynamic graph attention network. First， a fine-grained spatial solar irradiance identification method considering the influence of cloud thickness is developed using the partial thin-plate spline method， providing high-resolution solar irradiance data of 1 km×1 km for DPV stations. Subsequently， a graph attention network cell is employed to capture the spatiotemporal correlations of regional DPV power outputs under dynamically changing meteorological conditions by aggregating the neighborhood features of individual stations， while an encoder–decoder architecture is adopted to model the temporal evolution of the extracted spatial features. Finally， comparative experiments based on actual measured data from a region in Shanghai verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: DYPAL: Dynamic Privacy-Aware Split Learning for distributed medical imaging in IoMT networks
abstract: Training deep models on medical images is difficult because sensitive patient data is distributed across resource-constrained devices. This paper proposes DYPAL, a three-tier Dynamic Privacy-Aware Split Learning framework for IoMT systems. Devices transmit clipped, noised activations through edge and cloud tiers, applying differential privacy at the activation boundary. DYPAL exploits the link between split-point dimension and Gaussian noise energy. On a 15,000-image PathMNIST subset at ϵ ≈ 6 , reducing activation size from 2048 to 128 dimensions improves accuracy from 10.1% to 51.4% and cuts traffic by 91.7%. The gap is more than six times the largest seed-to-seed standard deviation we measure, so it is not run-to-run noise. Its Lyapunov controller reaches 40.3%, outperforming a 14.4% threshold heuristic.

title: Part Grounding, Not Action Knowledge: Locating the Bottleneck in VLM Affordance Prediction
abstract: Benchmarks agree that vision-language models reason poorly about low-level manipulation, but an aggregate accuracy score does not say which step fails. We separate two steps that affordance questions conflate: identifying which part of an object to act on, and knowing what action that part requires. Across 19 articulated objects we asked eight models, spanning three developers, what motion a robot should apply. Under an open prompt, push was produced once in 64 evaluations where it was correct, despite being correct for 8 of 19 objects and appearing in the offered label set every time. Inspecting the outputs showed why: models described a different part than the one being scored, e.g. explaining how to pick up a camera rather than press its button. Naming the target part raises action accuracy by 0.32 to 0.63 for every model, from 0.158-0.474 to 0.684-0.947, and push recall from 0-1/8 to 7-8/8. No model beats a constant answer that ignores the image under the open prompt; once the part is named, all eight do. Asked to describe the same part in free prose with no label set, models produce pressing language for 6 to 8 of 8. These results are hard to reconcile with missing action knowledge, and instead point to part grounding as the dominant bottleneck, a pattern that holds across all three model families and does not diminish with capability. Naming the part supplies the grounding variable, so this bounds what a perfect part detector would offer rather than demonstrating a general model of mechanics. Two supporting results agree: on real photographs only three of eight models localize grasp points better than a constant baseline, and on rendered objects none do. We also document two measurement errors of our own, a threshold that let a constant baseline score 0.929 and a labelling rule wrong on 4 of 19 objects, both caught only by testing our numbers against trivial alternatives.

title: Video2Reaction: Training Foundation Video Models to Predict Audience Reaction
abstract: We introduce Video2Reaction, a multimodal dataset that maps short movie segments to the induced emotional reactions of viewers in the wild, as expressed through social media comments. Video2Reaction captures the natural diversity of emotional responses by aggregating reactions from online comments at scale, modeling labels as distributions over categorical emotions to better reflect the subjective and ambiguous nature of emotional perception. We benchmark two vision-language models (VLMs) finetuned with LoRA, showing that VLMs learn effectively from Video2Reaction and outperform specialized baselines on dominant reaction prediction. We further demonstrate that VLMs pre-finetuned on Video2Reaction transfer effectively to VCE, another induced emotion dataset with a different taxonomy and video domain. Notably, LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B pre-finetuned on Video2Reaction and adapted on only 1% of VCE training data achieves a top-3 accuracy of 0.682, on par with the best reported VCE performance trained on the full dataset. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/infofusionlab/Video2Reaction

title: Support of Dyson Brownian Motion
abstract: We consider beta-Dyson Brownian motion, with β>= 1, started from a deterministic configuration with uniformly bounded support. Let μ_t be the semicircular free-convolution flow issued from the initial empirical measure, and set S_t = supp(μ_t). For every fixed T, ε> 0, with probability at least 1 - C exp(-(log n)^2), every particle remains within an epsilon-neighborhood of S_t for all 0 <= t <= T. The result holds from time zero, requires no regularity assumption at the initial spectral edges, and applies to multi-cut supports with macroscopic interior gaps. A key ingredient is a deterministic local resolvent exclusion principle: an o((n η)^(-1)) comparison of Stieltjes transforms on a complex disc above a real point separated from the reference support excludes eigenvalues from the corresponding real interval. This gives a model-independent mechanism for converting local resolvent estimates into spectral confinement.

title: Lifted-Product QLDPC Codes in the Polynomial Domain
abstract: This paper presents a finite-length polynomial-domain formulation of lifted-product quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes. We formulate the code construction over the quotient ring F 2[D]/(D L + 1), where polynomial base matrices are lifted entrywise to binary circulant blocks. This representation gives a compact algebraic description of the lifted-product parity-check matrices and allows CSS orthogonality to be analyzed before binary expansion. We show that the standard circulant lifting map is compatible with polynomial conjugation, which implies that the resulting binary matrices satisfy the CSS commutation constraint. The construction is illustrated with a constraint length 7, rate 1/2 NASA convolutional code example, and numerical examples are provided from a 3 x 4 polynomial parity-check matrix. The finite-length performance of selected constructed codes is then evaluated over the depolarizing channel using various benchmark decoders. The resulting framework gives a structured method to construct finite-length lifted-product QLDPC codes from small polynomial base matrices.

title: Linguocultural aspects of the attribution of a literary text (based on the material of "A Novel with Cocaine")
abstract: The object of this study is the linguocultural aspects of the attribution of a literary text, while the subject is the system of discourses through which they are realized, creating a real or imaginary image of its author. The research is conducted on the material of the text "A Novel with Cocaine," whose authorship has not yet been fully established. The aim of the study is to establish a connection between the linguocultural features of this novel and the presumed authorship of three contenders for it. The work examines in detail the system of discourses in this work, through which a real or imaginary image of the presumed author can be formed. Special attention is paid to the interrelationship between language markers that "reveal" its author(s) (features of vocabulary, syntax, figurative-expressive means, architecture, etc.) and the identification of culturally significant details: the realities of the era, autobiographical elements, the author's mentality, and the cultural codes of their environment. The following methods are employed in the study: descriptive, discourse analysis, linguocultural, autobiographical, semantic, and interpretative analysis. The scientific novelty lies in the fact that the work directly investigates the connection between linguocultural studies and the attribution of a literary text for the first time, where the attributed text is viewed as a holistic unity of language and culture, containing "traces" of its author, making it possible to judge them as a real person. The main conclusions of the study are that, firstly, "A Novel with Cocaine" is the quintessence of the "literary war" that took place at the turn of the 1920s and 1930s between V. Nabokov and his literary opponents, and secondly, this work, in the person of the main contender for its authorship, V. S. Yanovsky, represents a creative manifesto of the "unnoticed generation," demonstrating the ability to write in a beautiful classical literary tradition, which he was often criticized for neglecting.

title: Machine Learning and Ensemble Approaches for Sentiment Classification of Mobile Application Reviews
abstract: Mobile application marketplaces generate huge volumes of user reviews daily. Automatically understanding if a review is positive or negative matters to developers, platform operators, and prospective users alike, since manually reading them one by one is not feasible. This paper reviews the empirical and methodological literature on machine-learning-based sentiment classification, with particular attention to studies using Google Play Store review data. It synthesises a substantial body of empirical work and examines the preprocessing techniques that recur across it, which includes tokenization, count vectorization, TF-IDF, and transformer-based embeddings. It also discusses, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC, and also reviews the core classifiers used. The Support Vector Machines, Multinomial Naïve Bayes, AdaBoost, and ensemble strategies where applied. Three major challenges with the classification of Google Play Store where also discussed. The challenges include the systematic handling of emojis, principled handling of class imbalance, and statistical validation of reported performance gains. Together, these gaps motivate further research into ensemble architectures that combine classical classifiers with modern contextual embeddings for domain-specific, imbalanced, and informally written review text.

title: Typhon DB Sentry: Practical Queryable Column-Level Encryption with Fast Format-Preserving Decryption
abstract: Consultar dados mantendo-os cifrados é ferozmente difícil— exigências criptográficas, semânticas e de desempenho colidem. A cifragem em nível de coluna protege dados sensíveis contra adversários privilegiados, mas destrói as propriedades semânticas do SQL; quando se torna consultável, a agregação no proxy vira o gargalo, pois é preciso decifrar cada valor antes de agregá-lo. Apresentamos o Typhon DB Sentry, um proxy SQL transparente que torna dados cifrados por coluna consultáveis (faixa, padrão, ordenação, agregação) em PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle e IBM Db2, com as chaves fora da aplicação. A contribuição central da ferramenta é um caminho de decifragem rápida com preservação de formato: trocamos a aritmética de precisão arbitrária do FF1 (NIST) por uma implementação de largura fixa adaptativa—inteiros de 128 bits no caso comum, com fallback para inteiros grandes—byte-idêntica ao padrão, e deciframos grandes conjuntos de resultados em paralelo, fundindo decifragem e agregação em um único passo. Com o caminho completo, o SUM/AVG no proxy sobre 150K valores cifrados executa em ~0,08–0,12 s nos cinco dialetos (~1,6–18× sobre o texto claro; o caminho convencional decifra-e-agrega paga ~80×), sem alterar o texto cifrado. Demonstramos a ferramenta com uma aplicação web completa de clínica médica servida inteiramente através do proxy.

abstract: В статье исследуется развитие стратегического управления предприятиями на основе технологий искусственного интеллекта, предполагающее переход от локализованного применения интеллектуальных инструментов к их системной интеграции в процессы анализа, прогнозирования, распределения ресурсов и адаптивной корректировки стратегии. title: Does Understanding AI Internals Become Harder Faster Than Models Become More Capable
abstract: Mechanistic interpretability is often discussed as if progress in understanding models will naturally track progress in model capability, yet the evidence increasingly suggests that frontier models may become useful, general, and agentically competent faster than researchers can build causally faithful and globally valid accounts of how their internal computations produce those behaviors. Formalizing this tension as the interpretability scaling problem, we distinguish representation discovery from mechanistic understanding and argue that the relevant burden is not parameter count alone, but the product of effective feature inventory, causal interaction complexity, context and task coverage, and the cost of validating explanatory claims. Across sparse autoencoders, transcoders, circuit discovery, activation patching, and attribution graphs, recent work shows substantial scaling progress, yet the same literature exposes a widening validation problem: OpenAI reports that a 16-million-feature sparse autoencoder still leaves reconstruction and coverage gaps while anticipating that a comprehensive map may require billions or trillions of features, Gemma Scope infrastructures required massive stored activation and parameter scale, and circuit-tracing work on Claude 3.5 Haiku remains local, prompt-conditioned, and difficult to extend to long internal computations. We propose the Interpretability Scaling Gap (ISG), a measurable elasticity of mechanistic burden relative to effective interpretability capacity per unit capability gain. Our conclusion is conditional: for dense frontier systems, globally validated understanding currently appears to scale less favorably than capability, but automation, better evaluation, privileged high-level representations, and inspectable model designs can change the exponent - meaning the safety question is not whether a model can be explained at all, but whether verified explanatory coverage can keep pace with the expanding behavioral and causal surface that matters for deployment.

title: Pigeons That Learn to Flank You: A Critical Survey Review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of game AI and NPCs as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Probability Space Modeling with Adaptive Sampling
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic model for uncertainty representation and prediction, leveraging the principles of non-Euclidean geometry. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to effectively handle complex, high-dimensional systems with inherent uncertainty, relying on approximations that can lead to inaccurate predictions. This work proposes a model that explicitly incorporates a 'curvature' metric, dynamically adjusting sampling to maximize uncertainty and improve predictive accuracy. The core mechanism centers around a probabilistic framework where the model inherently guides the sampling process, offering a significant departure from standard Gaussian distributions. We detail the model's architecture, explain the rationale behind the curvature metric, and provide a comprehensive analysis of its performance on a challenging, multi-dimensional system. The research aims to address the limitations of existing probabilistic modeling techniques by providing a robust, adaptable, and potentially more accurate approach to uncertainty quantification, particularly within complex systems.

title: Algorithmic Self-Repair with Emergent Structure
abstract: This paper explores the concept of algorithmic self-repair, a novel approach to software development that leverages emergent structure to proactively address errors and enhance robustness. We propose a system centered around embedding a "self-diagnosis" mechanism within algorithms, capable of detecting and correcting errors through the propagation of corrections. This system utilizes a core logic that iteratively analyzes and refines the algorithm's structure, resulting in a self-correcting process. The core claim is that this design facilitates a significantly improved level of verification and error mitigation, moving beyond reactive verification methods.

title: Dynamic Programming for Adaptive Algorithm Selection
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithm selection that leverages the principles of dynamic programming. Traditional algorithm selection often relies on heuristics or hand-tuned strategies, which can be suboptimal and fail to adapt to varying problem characteristics. We argue that algorithm selection is fundamentally a sequential decision-making problem, analogous to optimization within dynamic programming. This work introduces a framework where a dynamic programming agent learns to select the optimal algorithm (or a combination thereof) based on a learned objective function. This objective function is continuously refined through a reinforcement learning process, taking into account factors such as input size, data distribution, and available computational budget. The core of the approach is a DP table that stores the best-known solution for subproblems, allowing for efficient exploration of the algorithm selection space. The system aims to achieve superior performance compared to static heuristics by dynamically adapting to the specific demands of each problem instance. The evaluation framework focuses on benchmarking the proposed method against established algorithms and heuristics on a suite of representative benchmark datasets. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the dynamic programming approach in adaptive algorithm selection.

title: ## Brydes Whale Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BWMOA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Brydes Whale Optimization Algorithm (BWMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Brydes whales. Brydes whales are known for their unique cooperative hunting strategy, where they utilize a specific communication protocol to locate prey. BWMOA leverages this strategy by employing a leader-follower approach with a dynamic communication mechanism. The algorithm's core components include a leader selection process based on fitness, a follower selection mechanism utilizing a communication range and probability, and an adaptive inertia weight mechanism. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a set of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. The objective is to improve upon existing metaheuristic algorithms through a more biologically-inspired approach, resulting in enhanced convergence speed and robustness. Key performance metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational cost are analyzed. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions and the algorithm's practical applications.

title: 拓扑信息论的量子计算的自适应纠错
abstract: 拓扑信息论是一种强大的数学工具,为描述和分析拓扑结构提供了框架。该理论在量子计算领域具有潜在的应用,尤其是在量子纠错方面。本研究旨在探索利用拓扑信息论构建量子纠错机制,旨在提高纠错效率并降低纠错的复杂度。本文将阐述核心概念,提出一个基于拓扑结构的自适应纠错算法,并对该算法的潜在优势进行分析。 我们的研究重点在于将拓扑结构作为纠错的依据,从而实现更高效的量子纠错,并有望解决量子计算中常见的纠错难题。

title: Dynamic Topological Abstraction with Quantum Entanglement Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational framework termed Dynamic Topological Abstraction (DTA) leveraging quantum entanglement. DTA proposes a mechanism where computational units dynamically form adaptive topological networks based on entangled states, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical bits and enabling parallel computations at unprecedented scales. The core of the framework relies on constructing reconfigurable topological networks through multi-body quantum entanglement. Each node represents a quantum state, and entanglement between nodes defines the topological connections. The strength of entanglement dictates the 'bandwidth' of the connection. Dynamic adjustment of entangled states allows the network topology to adapt to specific computational tasks, offering a fundamentally new approach to quantum computation. The proposed system aims to bridge the gap between the static nature of traditional topological computation and the hardware constraints of conventional quantum computing, with the potential for exponential performance gains. This work outlines the theoretical foundation and key design principles of DTA.

title: ## Black-tailed Antechinus-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Black-tailed Antechinus Algorithm (BTA), inspired by the foraging strategies and adaptive behaviors observed in *Callithrix margarita*, commonly known as the black-tailed antechinus. These marsupials exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting food resources in dynamic environments. The BTA leverages these principles, incorporating elements of exploration and exploitation to effectively navigate complex optimization landscapes. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search strategy, employing a 'trail' representation inspired by the antechinus's scent marking behavior to guide exploration. A 'fitness-dependent adaptation' mechanism mimics the animal's sensitivity to food availability, dynamically adjusting the exploration and exploitation parameters. The performance of the BTA is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's inherent adaptability and efficient exploration capabilities are key to its success. Further research will focus on refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its application in diverse problem domains.

title: CSLib: Building a Platform for AI-assisted Formal Verification in Lean
abstract: I’ll explain the new CSLib initiative, with a focus on its code reasoning effort, which aims to build a new industrial-strength formal verification platform in Lean for verifying real-world code. I’ll describe the principles and design decisions behind the CSLib code reasoning effort. I’ll then illustrate it with an end-to-end example that brings together: AI-assisted code generation and code specification; the Boole language and the Strata framework for language-agnostic code reasoning; trustworthy verification condition generation; and Lean automation through Lean-SMT and AI-assisted theorem proving.

title: Verifying Rust code with Verus
abstract: I will introduce Verus, an open-source, Rust-based verification tool aimed at concurrent software and systems software, which I develop together with a number of collaborators in academia and industry. Verus has spawned a number of publications on a range of verified systems, is already seeing industrial use at Microsoft and Amazon, and has been the subject of a number of experiments on generating proofs with AI. In this tutorial, I will give an overview of Verus and what it can do, and why we invented it compared to the previous state-of-the-art approaches to program verification. I will give a tutorial on how to get started with Verus, and I will illustrate how we approach the various challenges of verification through a number of examples.

title: Analisis Sentimen Ulasan Pelanggan Terhadap Tomoro Coffe Menggunakan Metode Random Forest Berbasis Text Mining
abstract: Using a Random Forest technique based on text mining, this research seeks to examine consumer sentiment about Tomoro Coffee reviews. There were a total of 927 reviews culled from various online sources; 546 were favorable and 381 were unfavorable. Data collection, sentiment labeling, and text preparation (including cleaning, stopword removal, tokenizing, and stemming) were the study steps that came before data transformation using TF-IDF. After then, the dataset was divided into two halves, with training and testing data comprising 80:20 of the total. The Random Forest method was then used for classification. The accuracy was 80.65%, precision was 83.58%, recall was 70.10%, and the F1-score was 79.50%, according to the test findings. It was clear from the confusion matrix that the model excelled at detecting positive emotion as opposed to negative. Good, comfortable, and pleasant were the most often used positive emotion terms in the word cloud, while application, voucher, promotion, and payment were the most commonly used negative sentiment words. Based on the findings, it seems that Tomoro Coffee's product and service quality may be evaluated using the Random Forest approach, which is based on text mining. This method is effective for categorizing customer review sentiment.

title: An Ontology of Explanation for Social eXplainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The recent surge of interest in eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has led to a growing focus on incorporating social insights into XAI and grounding explainability in social interaction. This has given rise to the concept of Social XAI. However, ontological modelling of the Social XAI framework remains limited. In particular, there is a lack of models that capture the progressivity of explanation processes in terms of the changes that occur. This paper introduces the Social XAI Ontology, a BFO-based reference ontology. The ontology models a variety of entities involved in the process of explanation. First, it provides a model of the participants in explanatory dialogues, such as artificial explainers and human explainees, and the roles they may take. Then, it introduces a rich set of explanatory moves that explainers and explainees perform. The paper further presents ontological accounts of four types of context that are central to real-world Social XAI projects. Furthermore, it provides an ontological account of different dimensions of adaptivity, which is considered to be an essential prerequisite for realizing Social XAI systems. Finally, the paper revisits two existing models of understanding in Social XAI by applying a recent theory of change. The paper concludes by discussing use cases for the Social XAI Ontology.

title: Privacy-Preserving AI Through Blockchain and Federated Learning
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems rely more on vast volumes of sensitive and personal data, ensuring that data privacy becomes crucial. Conventional centralized AI training techniques fail to comply with stringent legal standards and pose privacy hazards. This chapter introduces a novel privacy protection system that combines federated learning (FL) and blockchain technology to facilitate the use of decentralized, secure, and legally compliant AI. FL removes the requirement to distribute raw data by enabling model training directly on user devices or institutional data silos. FL, however, presents new difficulties about openness, trust, and the accuracy of model updates. Blockchain serves as a decentralized trust layer by providing verifiable update tracking, immutable logging, and the capacity to impose data governance standards through smart contracts. The proposed architecture provides a robust foundation for data protection, ensuring model performance is not compromised by incorporating additional privacy-enhancing technologies, including homomorphic encryption, secure multiparty computation, and differential privacy. This chapter represents one of the best-structured and most comprehensive studies that combines the concepts of FL, blockchain, and privacy-preserving mechanisms into a single chapter, thus contributing to research and acting as an educational reference for future research work.

title: On the Structural Optimization of Industrial Control Systems Using Metaheuristic Algorithms
abstract: The paper addresses the synthesis of a cost-optimal hardware architecture of the automated process control system (APCS) for continuous processes. The problem is formalized as the search for a minimum-cost rooted tree of devices subject to constraints on the number of I/O channels, the types and number of communication interfaces, the information capacity of processors, the regulation time and the reliability. The signals are grouped by control rooms. The problem is NP-hard, and a hybrid method is proposed that combines a deterministic hierarchy construction with a modified ant colony optimization (ACO) for device-type selection, enhanced by an adaptive heuristic. On ten instances the method is compared with a genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), simulated annealing (SA) and CP-SAT over 30 runs each. By the best found cost the hybrid ACO outperforms GA, PSO and SA on all instances with more than 100 IOs (by 14-38 %) and runs 9-14 times faster. By the median cost, however, the deterministic-greedy baselines are more reliable (GA attains the best Friedman rank) because the cost of the ACO runs is highly variable. All differences are confirmed by the Friedman and Wilcoxon tests. The method targets the early-design search for the cheapest feasible architecture and synthesizes one within minutes at industrial scale (A up to 1086).

title: Detector‐Frame Quantum Limits for Heterodyne Timing in Relativistic Optical Links
abstract: ABSTRACT Long‐baseline optical links for space interferometry and satellite quantum networks rely on heterodyne phase tracking under Doppler motion and gravitational frequency shifts. These relativistic shifts can generate large detector‐frame beat‐frequency offsets over finite readout windows and thereby constrain the temporal precision of front‐end phase readout. We develop a detector‐frame framework for this problem using an effective two‐mode signal–local‐oscillator model in which relativistic motion rescales the local‐oscillator frequency. Within this setting we derive closed‐form Mandelstam–Tamm and Margolus–Levitin bounds for representative Gaussian resources and connect global state distinguishability with the operational precision of heterodyne phase tracking. In the bright‐local‐oscillator regime we identify a geometric–operational mismatch: the joint optical state can evolve on arbitrarily short global timescales while the relevant information rate is set by the measured detector record. Combining this result with an open‐loop transient‐acquisition analysis, we show that white phase noise and relativistic beat‐frequency drift that is approximately constant over the acquisition window generate a cube‐root scaling benchmark for the optimal pre‐lock open‐loop integration window and the minimum residual phase error. These results establish detector‐frame benchmarks for quantum‐limited heterodyne timing in relativistic optical links and clarify how global dynamical bounds enter task‐restricted continuous optical measurements.
