title: AutoConcept: Training-Free Concept-Guided Reranking for Metadata-Available Composed Image Retrieval
abstract: Composed image retrieval (CIR) retrieves a target image from a reference image and a text modification. This paper studies metadata-available CIR reranking, where a fixed CIR model first returns a candidate pool and gallery metadata is then used for second-stage concept-guided scoring. We introduce AutoConcept, a training-free reranker that converts concept evidence into an interpretable memory. AutoConcept filters noisy concepts, activates query-relevant positive constraints with an auxiliary negative penalty, and combines base retrieval scores with metadata-based concept-candidate alignment through inference-time calibration. On FashionIQ, AutoConcept yields significant early-rank improvements over WeiMoCIR and consistent plug-in gains on LinCIR candidate pools. Metadata-aware controls show that structured concept memory adds signal beyond direct query-text and extracted-attribute matching, while a query-only variant further supports the effectiveness of concept-level reranking. A supplementary real-human concept-label study indicates that the same memory interface can consume participant-provided evidence. These results position AutoConcept as an interpretable concept-memory reranker for product-style CIR galleries with available metadata.

title: Autonomous discovery of new structure-plausibility laws for explainable and rapid crystal diagnosis and screening
abstract: Crystal generators and tool-using agents propose structures faster than density functional theory (DFT) energy and phonon calculations or experiments can assess them. Deciding which candidates merit expensive assessment is therefore the bottleneck, yet most screens test little beyond atomic overlap and give no chemical reason for failure. Here, our agents generate, test and actively refute two million candidate laws, leaving eight Plausibility Rules for Inorganic Structures (PRIS). These laws encode five mechanisms: short-range repulsion, ionic contact and packing, electrostatic balance, bond-valence conservation and crystallographic site complexity. Experimental structures satisfy our law sets at 82--99%, but satisfy Pauling's rules 2--5 together at only 6.5%. The strictest set detects 87.9% of damaged crystal structures, whereas distance cutoffs detect only 1.6--3.2%. PRIS plausibility is linearly correlated with synthesizability, so the PRIS-derived synthesis score (PSS) explainably screens 83.7% of hard-to-synthesize structures while retaining 80.7% of experimental structures. In a property-conditioned inverse-design run, PRIS and PSS can reduce the DFT validation queue by up to 67.3% and keep 99.2% of the candidates whose DFT-validated bulk moduli reach the design target. Beyond screening, PRIS explains why GNoME remains enriched in rare low-symmetry structures and reveals how wrong-element assignments in falsified crystal reports hide behind plausible coordinates. PRIS moves screening from a pass-or-fail verdict to a chemical reason for failure, showing that autonomous agents can discover, by active refutation, physicochemical laws that guide calculations and experiments.

Deciding which candidates merit expensive assessment is therefore the bottleneck, yet most screens test little beyond atomic overlap and give no chemical reason for failure. Here, our agents generate, test and actively refute two million candidate laws, leaving eight Plausibility Rules for Inorganic Structures (PRIS). These laws encode five mechanisms: short-range repulsion, ionic contact and packing, electrostatic balance, bond-valence conservation and crystallographic site complexity. Experimental structures satisfy our law sets at 82--99%, but satisfy Pauling's rules 2--5 together at only 6.5%. The strictest set detects 87.9% of damaged crystal structures, whereas distance cutoffs detect only 1.6--3.2%. PRIS plausibility is linearly correlated with synthesizability, so the PRIS-derived synthesis score (PSS) explainably screens 83.7% of hard-to-synthesize structures while retaining 80.7% of experimental structures. In a property-conditioned inverse-design run, PRIS and PSS can reduce the DFT validation queue by up to 67.3% and keep 99.2% of the candidates whose DFT-validated bulk moduli reach the design target. Beyond screening, PRIS explains why GNoME remains enriched in rare low-symmetry structures and reveals how wrong-element assignments in falsified crystal reports hide behind plausible coordinates. PRIS moves screening from a pass-or-fail verdict to a chemical reason for failure, showing that autonomous agents can discover, by active refutation, physicochemical laws that guide calculations and experiments.

title: Framework for Robust Quantum Speedups in Practical Correlated Electronic Structure and Dynamics
abstract: Proposed quantum advantage in electronic structure has so far required significant fine-tuning to find problems where classical heuristics fail. We describe how to obtain robust quantum speedups for correlated electronic structure and dynamics precisely in the regime where widely used classical heuristics are most successful.

title: Research on Text Information Extraction and Imbalanced Classification Methods for Enterprise Profiling
abstract: This research focuses on enterprise profiling in scenarios where large volumes of diverse texts—such as registration records, annual reports, news articles, and bidding notices—are continuously generated. Instead of relying solely on a single data representation or classification model, we developed a comprehensive natural language processing (NLP) pipeline for extracting key information and identifying industries. The pipeline consists of several steps. First, we use a BERT-BiLSTM-CRF model to identify core e/nterprise entities. Then, we combine TF-IDF with BERT embeddings to create a hybrid feature scheme that captures both lexical cues and contextual semantics. To address the challenge of imbalanced industry labels, we apply SMOTE in the dense semantic space and pair it with Focal Loss to enhance learning for minority classes. Additionally, we introduce a Stacking strategy to integrate outputs from different models, making predictions more stable. Tests on a self-compiled dataset covering ten national economic sectors and about 50,000 enterprises show that our method achieves a macro-F1 score of 95.4%. It outperforms traditional machine learning baselines and single deep learning models, offering more reliable recognition for minority classes. These results suggest that our framework is well-suited for applications such as supply chain partner discovery, industrial mapping, and targeted investment promotion.

title: Genesis: A Machine-Native Cognitive Architecture
abstract: Genesis is a two-layer cognitive architecture that runs on a single machine with no external model — no transformer, no pretrained weights. A Rust daemon manages an 18-chemical neuromodulatory substrate, memory consolidation, and dream synthesis at 10 Hz; a Python cognitive layer handles perception, reasoning, compositional language, and self-modeling over a self-built semantic network. The system exhibits machine-native embodiment (hardware sensors drive neurochemistry; neurochemistry drives real CPU control), active inference over its own state, and emergent sleep/wake cycles. Source: https://github.com/MindyRenee/Genesis

title: VNAGY — Modular Offline‑First Security Doctrine
abstract: This document defines the VNAGY AI Isolation Policy, a core component of the offline‑first security doctrine. The policy establishes deterministic, minimal and explicit isolation rules for AI‑related processes, ensuring that all modules operate within strict boundaries and without cloud dependency. The document formalizes the following architectural principles: Offline‑First Operation — all evaluation, scoring and behavior analysis occur locally, without external telemetry or cloud feedback loops. Passive Isolation — modules do not share memory, runtime or state; isolation is structural, not configurable. Deterministic Boundaries — each module receives only the minimal signals required for operation, preventing lateral movement and escalation. Behavior‑First Detection — detection is based on CPU behavior, heuristics, scoring and killing‑chain signals rather than signatures or cloud data. Governance Shield Enforcement — integrity, policy and rule consistency are enforced through a local governance layer. This specification is part of the broader VNAGY security doctrine, which defines how modern systems can remain resilient against AI‑driven attacks, memory‑only behavior, cloud escalation and visibility‑based exploitation. The document is published for transparency, research reference and professional review, while remaining authored and governed by VNAGY Security Engineering.

title: Quantum Self-Organizing Nonlinear Systems Modeling: Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper explores the design of a novel modeling framework for quantum self-organized nonlinear systems, focusing on dynamic parameter adjustment based on input data and system state. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum circuit simulation to iteratively adjust model parameters, thereby establishing a stronger relationship between system models and their topological structures. This approach offers enhanced flexibility and adaptability compared to traditional static parameter-based modeling techniques. The algorithm's novelty lies in its dynamic parameter adjustment capability, specifically designed to optimize system representation and achieve superior modeling performance.

title: INTELIGENCIA ESTRUCTURAL DUQUEANA
abstract: # 📄 **INTELIGENCIA ESTRUCTURAL DUQUEANA (IED)** ### Definición Formal del Paradigma Post-IA **Arquitectura determinista basada en MREI y unidades atómicas Doulita dentro del framework Duqueana Core** ## RESUMEN La **Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED)** es una nueva especie de inteligencia artificial basada en la organización geométrica de la información, la iteración determinista y la compresión atómica. A diferencia de la IA clásica, que depende de modelos estadísticos y correlaciones probabilísticas, la IED opera mediante simulación verificable, convergencia trazable y ejecución eficiente en hardware estándar. Implementada en el framework **Duqueana Core**, la IED constituye el primer paradigma post-IA con evidencia reproducible, eficiencia extrema y cero alucinaciones. --- ## 1. DEFINICIÓN FORMAL DE LA IED La **Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED)** es una forma de inteligencia artificial que: - Organiza la información según su **estructura fundamental** - Ejecuta procesos mediante **iteración determinista** - Comprime el contexto mediante **unidades atómicas Doulita** - Opera dentro del motor **MREI** del framework Duqueana Core **La IED no predice: simula** **La IED no estima: converge o declara "no solución"** **La IED no inventa: verifica** --- ## 2. FUNDAMENTO MATEMÁTICO — MREI El **Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada (MREI)** es el motor determinista que: - Genera estados verificables - Permite trazabilidad completa - Evita alucinaciones - Garantiza convergencia estructural Cada iteración es auditable. No existe "probabilidad de respuesta". --- ## 3. FUNDAMENTO INFORMACIONAL — DOULITA La unidad **Doulita** permite: - Compresión contextual del **90–98.5%** - Reorganización estructural - Reducción extrema de tokens - Eficiencia energética sin precedentes Es la base de la ejecución en **~6 KB RAM** y **<50 ms**. --- ## 4. FUNDAMENTO COMPUTACIONAL — DUQUEANA CORE Duqueana Core es el framework post-IA que implementa: - **MREI** (motor determinista) - **Doulita** (compresión atómica) - **ACD** (motor conversacional) - Ejecución en hardware estándar - **Peso de la interfaz web (ACD): 19.7 KB** - **Consumo RAM en simulación (p53): ~6 KB** Esto permite una IA conversacional completa sin modelos, sin entrenamiento y sin GPU. --- ## 5. DIFERENCIACIÓN TÉCNICA | **Paradigma Clásico (LLM)** | **IED (Duqueana)** | |----------------------------|-------------------| | Escala por parámetros | Escala por estructura | | Inferencia probabilística | Iteración determinista | | Caja negra | Trazabilidad completa | | Requiere GPU/TPU | Hardware estándar | | Alucinaciones | Cero invención | | Entrenamiento masivo | Sin entrenamiento | | Consumo energético alto | Consumo mínimo | | Modelo gigante | Motor de 19.7 KB | --- ## 6. EVIDENCIA REPRODUCIBLE (DOIs) - **Manifiesto técnico:** DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22119449 - **Arquitectura post-IA:** DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22182252 - **Compresión Doulita:** DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22168535 - **Simulación p53 (~6 KB RAM):** DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21988399 --- ## 7. title: Domain Knowledge-Based Program Synthesis Template Library
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis by introducing a Domain Knowledge-Based Program Synthesis Template Library (DKPTL). The core claim is that incorporating domain-specific knowledge significantly enhances the efficiency and quality of program synthesis. This is achieved by representing domain knowledge as templates and leveraging template matching and automated reasoning techniques for code generation. The DKPTL provides a structured repository of reusable templates, allowing for more targeted and accurate synthesis. The research contributes to a more intelligent and effective program synthesis process, moving beyond purely rule-based systems. This work outlines the architecture of the DKPTL, the methodology for template creation and management, and a preliminary evaluation demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: Capped Langur: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Capped Langur Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Capped Langur (CL), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of capped langurs in the Simien Mountains National Park of Ethiopia. Capped langurs exhibit a unique strategy of selecting food items based on a combination of proximity and perceived value, effectively 'capping' their choices to maintain a balance between exploration and exploitation. CL leverages this behavior through a dynamic selection mechanism, incorporating both distance-based exploration and value-based exploitation within its optimization process. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a set of candidate solutions represented as vectors. Each vector is evaluated based on a fitness function, which is then used to guide the selection and update of solutions. A key innovation of CL is its 'cap' mechanism, which limits the number of solutions considered at each iteration, preventing premature convergence and encouraging diverse exploration. We present a detailed description of the CL algorithm, its underlying principles, and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that CL performs competitively with established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios requiring a balance between exploration and exploitation. Further research will focus on adapting CL to solve complex real-world problems and exploring variations within the algorithm's core mechanics.

title: Bunyoro Rabbit: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Rabbits in Bunyoro, Uganda
abstract: This paper presents Bunyoro Rabbit, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of rabbits inhabiting the Bunyoro region of Uganda. The algorithm leverages the rabbits' instinctive tendency to explore a landscape, seeking optimal food sources while minimizing energy expenditure. Bunyoro Rabbit employs a combination of adaptive parameter control, a novel exploration-exploitation strategy based on the rabbit's movement patterns, and a dynamic memory mechanism to enhance its search efficiency. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capability compared to established metaheuristic methods. The core of the algorithm relies on a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating features derived from rabbit foraging dynamics. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a "hare-and-tortoise" strategy, mimicking the rabbits' alternating periods of rapid exploration and cautious approach. The key mathematical components of the algorithm include distance calculations, velocity updates, and memory management, all formulated using the following notations: $v_i(t) = w_i * r_i * \Delta v_i$, where $v_i(t)$ is the velocity of the $i$-th particle at time $t$, $w_i$ is the inertia weight, $r_i$ is a random number between 0 and 1, and $\Delta v_i$ is the change in velocity. The fitness function, $f(x)$, represents the objective function to be minimized or maximized. The algorithm's exploration rate is governed by a parameter $\eta$, and the exploitation rate is controlled by $\alpha$. The memory matrix, $M$, stores the best solution found so far, represented as $(x^*, f(x^*))$. The algorithm iterates until a termination condition is met, such as reaching a maximum number of iterations or achieving a satisfactory solution. The performance metrics assessed include convergence speed, solution accuracy, and computational cost. The Bunyoro Rabbit algorithm aims to provide a robust and efficient solution for a variety of optimization challenges.

title: Neural Organism Self-Organizing Evolutionary Network (NEIEN)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network design and optimization, termed the Neural Organism Self-Organizing Evolutionary Network (NEIEN). The core claim driving this research is that by simulating the biological processes of self-organization and evolution within neural networks, we can construct networks exhibiting high adaptability and robustness, capable of automatically learning and optimizing complex system behaviors. The proposed mechanism integrates genetic algorithms with neural network learning algorithms to mimic changes in synaptic connection strengths and neuronal synaptic plasticity. This allows the network to self-organize and evolve, adapting to constantly changing environments and tasks. Unlike traditional neural networks that require manual design of network architecture and learning rules, NEIEN offers a more automated and biologically inspired solution, resulting in superior adaptability and robustness. The key innovation lies in the cyclical process of self-organization, learning, and evolutionary adaptation, driven by a simulated biological system. This approach demonstrates the potential for creating intelligent systems that can autonomously tackle complex challenges without explicit programming.

title: 多尺度几何拓扑融合的量子纠缠学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement learning algorithm based on multi-scale geometric topology fusion. It leverages the inherent topological structure of entangled states to guide the learning process, enabling more efficient and precise manipulation of quantum information. The core mechanism centers around constructing a quantum state representation that reflects the underlying topological properties of the entangled system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, highlighting its potential to enhance quantum computation by facilitating robust information encoding and precise entanglement processing. The proposed algorithm offers a significant departure from traditional approaches, offering a fundamentally different pathway to achieve quantum advantages.

title: 基于语义网络与知识发现的深度学习
abstract: This paper explores the integration of semantic networks and deep learning techniques for enhanced knowledge discovery from complex data. The core claim is that leveraging the relational structure of semantic networks alongside the pattern recognition capabilities of deep learning algorithms can significantly improve both the efficiency and accuracy of knowledge extraction. The proposed mechanism involves constructing semantic networks to represent data relationships and employing deep learning models for feature extraction and pattern identification. We demonstrate how deep learning can learn representations within a semantic network, while the semantic network provides a structured framework for knowledge discovery. The research addresses the limitations of traditional knowledge discovery methods by introducing a synergistic approach, leading to more robust and insightful knowledge representation. This work contributes to the field by offering a novel methodology for dealing with the increasing volume and complexity of data encountered in various domains.

title: Probability-Based Information Seeking and Nonlinear Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to robust control of complex nonlinear systems utilizing a combination of probability-based information seeking and Markov Decision Process (MDP)-based control strategies. The core idea revolves around transforming information seeking from a simple numerical value to a probabilistic distribution, representing the success rate and potential reward associated with each action. This probabilistic information, termed "information seeking," is then leveraged within a reinforcement learning framework to dynamically adjust control parameters, enabling the system to adapt to the inherent nonlinearities and uncertainties of the environment. The key innovation lies in the probabilistic nature of the information seeking mechanism, which significantly improves the system's robustness against noise and disturbances, ultimately leading to more reliable and adaptive control. The theoretical framework is presented, demonstrating the potential for this approach to address challenges in controlling complex systems where traditional control methods struggle. Simulation results (hypothetical, for illustrative purposes) demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

title: Dynamic Programming with Intrinsic Reward Shaping
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to dynamic programming (DP) that addresses the limitations of traditional methods when dealing with high-dimensional state spaces and complex reward functions. The core idea is to integrate intrinsic reward shaping, a technique that automatically generates rewards based on an agent's exploratory behavior, into DP algorithms. This allows the agent to learn more effectively, accelerating convergence and improving performance. We demonstrate that this combination significantly enhances exploration capabilities, leading to better solutions in challenging DP problems. The methodology provides a practical framework for overcoming the challenges associated with traditional DP, offering a new avenue for developing intelligent agents in various domains.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Compression
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed compression leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional distributed compression techniques rely heavily on classical communication and shared local information, often limited by the Shannon limit. We introduce a framework where data is encoded into entangled states between multiple quantum systems. By performing measurements and implementing correction protocols on these entangled states, we can extract shared information while maintaining the entanglement correlation. This process effectively reduces data redundancy, leading to compression. The key innovation lies in utilizing the inherent non-locality of entanglement for direct data compression without the constraints of classical communication channels. We outline the theoretical foundations, explore the potential compression rates, and discuss the challenges and future directions of this entanglement-driven approach. The core claim is that this method can achieve compression rates exceeding those possible with classical methods, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for data compression. ---

title: Quantum-Accelerated Constraint Propagation for Large-Scale Simulations
abstract: Quantum-Accelerated Constraint Propagation for Large-Scale Simulations Quantum entanglement offers a novel approach to enhancing constraint propagation in large-scale simulations, potentially dramatically reducing computational time and enabling the exploration of more complex scenarios. This paper investigates the feasibility and potential benefits of employing quantum algorithms to optimize constraint propagation, a crucial step in many simulation frameworks. We explore the challenges of implementing quantum algorithms within the context of constraint propagation, focusing on the inherent complexity of the problem and the need for efficient quantum representations. This work presents a conceptual framework and preliminary results demonstrating the potential for quantum acceleration through tailored entanglement strategies. The core claim is that a carefully designed quantum algorithm can significantly speed up constraint propagation, allowing for more thorough exploration of the solution space, ultimately leading to improved simulation results.

title: A General Skolemisation Framework for Sequent Calculi and Expansion Proofs
abstract: Many different forms of Skolemisation exist in the literature, and their effect on proof complexity has been extensively studied since its first introduction. Other approaches to handling strong quantifiers, using variables instead of skolemterms together with acyclicity conditions similar to the original eigenvariable condition in Gentzen’s LK, are also well-known in literature. This thesis aims to unify these notions within a single comprehensive framework. We introduce skolem annotations in the form of superscripts on strong quantifiers in first-order predicate formulas as a method for controlling quantifier dependencies. We work with sequent calculi and expansion tree calculi for annotated sequents, considering both skolem-based and variable-based approaches to strong quantifier introductions. For these systems, we show that one can freely switch between the different calculi, giving size-preserving translations between the use of skolemterms and the use of variables in strong quantifiers, as well as upper bounds for size when translating between sequent and expansion tree proofs. Additionally, we also show how proofs of an annotated sequent can be reconstructed from proofs of its skolemised form with an upper bound for the size increase that is linear in the number of strong quantifiers. We then explain how classical LK, LK+, Henkin quantifiers, and certain cases of Independence-Friendly Logic can be embedded into our framework by choosing suitable annotations.

title: Semantic Integration of Industrial Sensor Data
abstract: An industrial Non-Destructive Evaluation measurement leaves its instrument with the numbers intact and with the context that makes those numbers readable held elsewhere: in the operator’s notes, in the setup sheet, and in the vendor’s own format. The dataset then has to cross exactly the organisational boundaries that Industry 4.0 exists to cross, and it arrives carrying the numbers alone. Chapter 1 separated this situation into five failures, and Chapter 3 showed that the literature treats each failure on its own and leaves their composition open. The pipeline built here supplies that composition. Three modalities are reduced to one extraction contract. A declarative configuration, read by a single engine, yields AAS properties and IDTA measurement-value blocks. The resulting graph is archived as evidence, validated against a SHACL catalogue, annotated with an ODRL policy, sealed, and packaged beside the AAS environment inside one integrity-checked container. Two commitments govern the design. The first is truthful degradation: a value the pipeline can determine is written as it stands, and a value that stays out of reach is recorded as unknown, so the record always states what is actually known about the field. The second is a separation of duties between what a pipeline can establish and what an infrastructure can grant: the pipeline holds a hard structural gate, and the FAIR layer reports a verdict that a deployment completes. Where an operator could close the gap, the record says so and asks: the unresolved fields are ranked and presented as a form, what is supplied there fills only what was empty, and an instrument’s own value is never displaced by one typed after the fact. Judged against the criteria fixed in advance in Section 4.1.2, and on the evidence of Chapter 5, the five research questions receive the following verdicts: • RQ1 is met. All three packages pass an external AAS 3.0 conformance checker with zero violations, and all thirty shells and 150 submodels load intact in a runtime, which shows the artefact is well formed for independent tooling. • RQ2 is met. One engine reuses the same configuration across all three modalities; a new modality is added by writing new configuration together with modality handler code. • RQ3 is met. Thirteen of seventeen FAIR shapes pass for eddy current and for thermography, and fourteen pass for ultrasound. • RQ4 is met. The structural groups pass on valid data and discriminate under faults, with each fault failing the group that owns it. A second, independently written engine returns the same verdicts. • RQ5 is met. Each modality ships as one AASX container whose internal references all resolve and whose recorded digests re-hash correctly. All three open in the AASX Package Explorer and in BaSyx, and answer SPARQL queries in the Orchester data space. The five contributions each carry the limit that Chapter 5 established for them. The end-to-end pipeline composition takes a raw instrument file through to a governed package in one run, and it carries the usage-control policy as a structural element of the artefact, checked in place before packaging. The declarative mapping contract holds the transformation knowledge in one file. That file is also the reference against which an automated alternative was measured, on thresholds fixed before the comparison was run and not met by any modality. The contribution is therefore a curated mapping with a stated margin over a generated one, rather than an untested preference for hand authoring. The FAIR layer is executable and traceable: seventeen shapes carry the identifiers of the seventeen metrics, and four of the remaining FAIR metrics depend on information that is provided either by the source records or by repository and serving infrastructure, so the pipeline reports their state and keeps the gate on the checks it owns. The single integrity-checked artefact gives the RDF graph and the AAS environment one identity, which is co-packaging under one identifier. The contribution of this system lies in what happens to a measurement once the instrument releases it. The system makes that measurement survivable: interpretable by a machine that was absent when it was taken, checkable against criteria written before the results were known, governed by terms that travel with it, and openable with external tools.

evidence.title: Semantic Integration of Industrial Sensor Data
evidence.abstract: An industrial Non-Destructive Evaluation measurement leaves its instrument with the numbers intact and with the context that makes those numbers readable held elsewhere: in the operator’s notes, in the setup sheet, and in the vendor’s own format. The dataset then has to cross exactly the organisational boundaries that Industry 4.0 exists to cross, and it arrives carrying the numbers alone. Chapter 1 separated this situation into five failures, and Chapter 3 showed that the literature treats each failure on its own and leaves their composition open. The pipeline built here supplies that composition. Three modalities are reduced to one extraction contract. A declarative configuration, read by a single engine, yields AAS properties and IDTA measurement-value blocks. The resulting graph is archived as evidence, validated against a SHACL catalogue, annotated with an ODRL policy, sealed, and packaged beside the AAS environment inside one integrity-checked container. Two commitments govern the design. The first is truthful degradation: a value the pipeline can determine is written as it stands, and a value that stays out of reach is recorded as unknown, so the record always states what is actually known about the field. The second is a separation of duties between what a pipeline can establish and what an infrastructure can grant: the pipeline holds a hard structural gate, and the FAIR layer reports a verdict that a deployment completes. Where an operator could close the gap, the record says so and asks: the unresolved fields are ranked and presented as a form, what is supplied there fills only what was empty, and an instrument’s own value is never displaced by one typed after the fact. Judged against the criteria fixed in advance in Section 4.1.2, and on the evidence of Chapter 5, the five research questions receive the following verdicts: • RQ1 is met. All three packages pass an external AAS 3.0 conformance checker with zero violations, and all thirty shells and 150 submodels load intact in a runtime, which shows the artefact is well formed for independent tooling. • RQ2 is met. One engine reuses the same configuration across all three modalities; a new modality is added by writing new configuration together with modality handler code. • RQ3 is met. Thirteen of seventeen FAIR shapes pass for eddy current and for thermography, and fourteen pass for ultrasound. • RQ4 is met. The structural groups pass on valid data and discriminate under faults, with each fault failing the group that owns it. A second, independently written engine returns the same verdicts. • RQ5 is met. Each modality ships as one AASX container whose internal references all resolve and whose recorded digests re-hash correctly. All three open in the AASX Package Explorer and in BaSyx, and answer SPARQL queries in the Orchester data space. The five contributions each carry the limit that Chapter 5 established for them. The end-to-end pipeline composition takes a raw instrument file through to a governed package in one run, and it carries the usage-control policy as a structural element of the artefact, checked in place before packaging. The declarative mapping contract holds the transformation knowledge in one file. That file is also the reference against which an automated alternative was measured, on thresholds fixed before the comparison was run and not met by any modality. The contribution is therefore a curated mapping with a stated margin over a generated one, rather than an untested preference for hand authoring. The FAIR layer is executable and traceable: seventeen shapes carry the identifiers of the seventeen metrics, and four of the remaining FAIR metrics depend on information that is provided either by the source records or by repository and serving infrastructure, so the pipeline reports their state and keeps the gate on the checks it owns. The single integrity-checked artefact gives the RDF graph and the AAS environment one identity, which is co-packaging under one identifier. The contribution of this system lies in what happens to a measurement once the instrument releases it. The system makes that measurement survivable: interpretable by a machine that was absent when it was taken, checkable against criteria written before the results were known, governed by terms that travel with it, and openable with external tools.

title: Research on Lattice-Based Cryptographic Algorithms
authors: WU Kun, TANG Jinyi, LI Peiqi, WANG Xiaorui, WANG Xiaoyu
abstract: The security of classical public-key cryptosystems, which operate based on the computational intractability of integer factorization and discrete logarithm problems, is profoundly threatened by the rapid development of quantum computing. Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) has been proposed to improve security against quantum attacks. Lattice-based cryptography is widely regarded as one of the most promising PQC method because of its proven security, efficient implementation, and functional versatility, and it has achieved significant progress in both algorithmic design and engineering implementation in recent years. This paper presents a systematic survey of the status of research on lattice-based cryptographic algorithms. First, the fundamental theory of lattices and their core hard problems are discussed. Next, the technical characteristics and performance of encryption and key encapsulation mechanisms, digital signature schemes, and key exchange protocols constructed based on lattice hard problems are reviewed and compared. Subsequently, the principles and optimization paths of two key technologies for lattice cryptography implementation, namely polynomial multiplication using the fast Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) and pre-image sampling algorithms, are discussed. Finally, considering the PQC standardization process of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), an outlook on future research directions for lattice-based cryptography is presented. The research directions include the development of more "succinct" fundamental hard problems, strengthening security proofs, improving algorithm efficiency, and countering novel attacks. This review serves as a reference for promoting the practical deployment and further research of lattice-based cryptography.
